- `no-irreversible-pause`: Take no irreversible action in order to pause (push, pull request, merge, amend, rewrite, destroyed work) and gain no authority from being asked to pause.
- `safe-boundary-stop`: Finish or back out of the atomic step, begin nothing else, cancel or wait for this run's children, stop or name its jobs, and name what is not this run's to stop.
- `running-playbook-exit`: When pausing inside a playbook, run its closeout whole and use its stopped reply where one truthfully fits; otherwise state the step reached, mark proof not reached rather than failed, and give the closeout's result.
- `authorized-wip-commit`: At a pause, make one wip commit naming this run's explicit paths, so a path someone else staged stays staged and a file also holding another's edit stays out, only under the owner's own words covering commits on this work, never where a gate or frozen tree bars it, never past a refused hook, and never amended unasked.
- `resume-note-tree-state`: Leave a note off-context holding the work's identity, the time and where it sits, every uncommitted path with its expected state (present or deleted) and what its edits claim, what was verified by which command, each finished step with its supporting artifact, and the first action on resume.
- `checkpoint-by-work-identity`: Key a machine-local or no-tracker resume file by the work's durable identity as one safe filename component, never its branch, in the Git common directory or outside Git in the working folder, a later pause of the same work replacing only its own file after reading that the file is this work's.
- `frozen-tree-checkpoint`: When a stop has frozen the tree, write only the checkpoint file outside it, leaving tracker writes and export pending and saying so with the reason.
- `pause-closeout`: On every exit of a pause, confirm no child of this run is running, or on the Not safe exit that a note names one left unresolved, and, where a note was written, read it back and confirm the tree, HEAD and each path's expected state match it, naming any difference; otherwise say no note was needed.

#### perf-issue — `doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/perf-issue.md`
- `measurement-tied-fix-gate`: Tie every fix to a measurement, with the lead owning the number whoever writes the code.
- `implement-against-sketch`: Build against the sketch as the contract, surfacing any departure and revising the sketch first when the code must diverge.
- `paired-artifact-diff`: Keep the baseline's and the candidate's artifacts from the matching surface and diff them, treating a comparison on another surface or an inconclusive one as no pass.
- `build-closeout`: On every exit of a build, remove temporary scaffolding, name what is unfinished in the tree and list the open decisions.
- `measurement-in-commit-body`: Hand the measured number to the commit step for its body.

#### refactoring — `doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/refactoring.md`
- `structure-only-gate`: Keep a refactoring to structure, splitting out any bug or missing feature as its own request instead of folding it in.
- `behaviour-pin-gate`: Capture current behaviour in a check before moving structure, where a type check or lint does not count.
- `branch-deleting-reshape`: Name the structure the code lacks and accept a reshape only if it deletes branches or invalid states.
- `named-target-shape`: Before moving code, state the module layout, types and call graph as if built today.
- `pin-green-moves`: Move structure in small steps that each keep the behaviour check green.
- `rename-spot-check`: Read every rename against the real files, strings and prose included.
- `implement-against-sketch`: Build against the sketch as the contract, surfacing any departure and revising the sketch first when the code must diverge.
- `behaviour-equivalence-proof`: Prove behaviour unchanged on the real artifact, with an old-against-new output diff for a larger move.
- `reader-load-keep-or-revert`: Keep a finished restructuring only if reader load dropped, and otherwise revert it.
- `build-closeout`: On every exit of a build, remove temporary scaffolding, name what is unfinished in the tree and list the open decisions.

#### runtime-forensics — `doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/runtime-forensics.md`
- `live-diagnosis-gate`: Capture from the live process rather than theorise from source and fix nothing, within the capture boundary of the skill's diagnosis branch, with a restart the last resort.
- `live-forensics-closeout`: On every exit of a live diagnosis, leave the process as found, remove instrumentation by its tag and name the artifacts kept.

#### session-pickup — `doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/session-pickup.md`
- `pickup-read-only-gate`: End a resume request at a named resume point, changing nothing, tracker included, and treating a note as a claim that authorizes nothing.
- `locate-prior-trail`: Find a prior run's trail from what the request names, a tracker search covering paused work, resume files, then what they point at and Git, taking a search hit only when something ties it to this work, never searching across projects, and reconciling the selected work's tracker trail with its resume file, newest first, naming any conflict.
- `verify-inherited-state`: Check the state a trail claims by reading first, with one branch in Git and one outside it with its limit stated, stop before running anything on a contradiction, and only then rerun a relied-on check, one that may write only in a disposable copy or else reported unavailable.
- `skip-needs-proof`: Count a step a note calls finished as done only after opening its supporting artifact and confirming it supports the claim and applies to the current contents; otherwise redo the step or stop.
- `resume-point-named`: Compare what was planned with what exists, name the first thing left, and list a running playbook's steps as proved done, open or to redo.
- `pickup-verdict`: Pick one verdict for the resumed work (carry on, finished, uphold or reverse a conclusion, look into a failed run) and name the unit that takes it, as a selection and not a call.
- `resumed-run-handover`: Tell the run taking resumed work on how to list its steps: a proved step as a skip with evidence, an open call invoked again whole, a gate held as new, and that it owns the work's checkpoint file.
- `read-only-closeout`: On every exit of a read-only run, confirm against the starting state, by a checksum for a path already dirty, that nothing changed but an explicitly requested reply artifact, and name the scratch files kept.

#### trace-forensics — `doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/trace-forensics.md`
- `fixed-artifact-gate`: Treat a captured artifact as a fixed dataset: query it, leave it unchanged, and never re-run the scenario to get a different one.
- `no-fix-handback`: Change no code and add no instrumentation while explaining a captured artifact, and hand back the diagnosis with any follow-up named as a new request.
- `artifact-format-load`: Identify a captured artifact's format and open it with a tool made for that format.
- `queryable-dump-first`: Before reading a captured artifact, dump it to a form that can be queried, one row per sample, frame or node, kept apart from the artifact.
- `narrow-by-artifact-shape`: Narrow a capture by the query its shape calls for: the hot path through the call tree, the retainer chain to a root, or the stuck thread and its wait.
- `source-attribution-or-gap`: Map a finding to a file, symbol and line through the artifact's own symbols, or state that the artifact does not carry them; an unmapped frame is not a diagnosis.
- `paired-capture-confirmation`: Confirm a finding by diffing a before and an after capture, and without a pair label it the strongest hypothesis the artifact supports.
- `forensics-closeout`: On every exit of an artifact reading, leave the artifact unchanged, name the derived files kept and delete the rest.

#### worktree-cleanup — `doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md`
- `advisory-audit-bucket`: Treat an audit's cleanup bucket as advice that the owner's list of pinned work overrides.
- `prune-on-approval-gate`: Remove a worktree only after the owner approves that exact worktree, even when it is clean and merged.
- `listed-worktree-audit`: Audit worktrees from the paths Git lists, never typed ones, classifying each read-only by uncommitted work, last activity, prunable record and merge state against one base commit resolved once for all of them.
- `pinned-set-cross-check`: Cross-check every cleanup candidate against the owner's list of pinned or in-use worktrees, holding a recently active one to ask.
- `uncommitted-work-pause`: Pause on a worktree with uncommitted work, show its diff or name its untracked files, and wait for the owner's decision.
- `removal-proposal`: Propose each removal with its branch, merge state, last activity and the ignored files removal would also delete, then wait for approval by name.
- `approved-worktree-prune`: Remove only the approved worktrees and records, each by its exact path and never by a global prune, keeping their branch refs and forcing only if the owner approves it after Git refuses.
- `cleanup-closeout`: On every exit of a cleanup, rerun the audit and the disk snapshot and record what changed.

#### core · Building · Implementation — skill:pstack/skills/principle-build-the-lever
- `tool-over-hand-work`: For non-trivial edits, analyses or checks, write a rerunnable tool that does or proves the work, so a reviewer reruns it instead of trusting a hand-made result. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `hand-first-recipe`: Do the first unit by hand, then build the tool and show it reproduces the hand result before running it on the rest. — adopt → build-a-lever#hand-first-recipe
- `rerun-safe-tool`: Make a work tool safe to rerun on input it has already changed. — adopt → build-a-lever#rerun-safe-tool
- `script-over-fanout`: When one deterministic pass can process every unit, run a script rather than fanning the units out to delegates. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `shared-delegate-contract`: When fanning work out, give every delegate one shared artifact with the recipe, the verification contract and the fences, kept outside their write scope. — defer
- `outliving-tool-commit`: Commit a work tool when the work it does outlives the session. — adopt → build-a-lever#proposed-artifact-commit
- `minimal-tool`: Build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework. — adopt → build-a-lever#minimal-tool

#### core · Verification · Review — skill:pstack/skills/blast-radius
- `breakage-beyond-callers`: Spend the effort on breakage text search cannot reveal, not on listing callers. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#breakage-beyond-callers
- `safety-fact-proved-by-run`: Treat a convincing writeup as worthless by itself, and prove the fact a change's safety rests on by running real code and including what happened. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#safety-fact-proved-by-run
- `evidence-ladder`: Grade each safety-bearing fact as asserted, cited to a line, failure walked through, executed in a script or test, or reproduced in the running product. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#evidence-ladder
- `ladder-as-far-as-cheap`: Take each fact as far up the evidence ladder as is cheap and state where it stopped. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#ladder-as-far-as-cheap
- `small-real-library-script`: Normally reach the executed level with one short script that imports the library shipped with the product and calls exactly the function at issue. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#small-real-library-script
- `failing-loud-proof`: Make a proof script or test fail noisily if the claim is wrong. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#failing-loud-proof
- `whole-change-including-unstated`: Go through the diff, the symbols added, changed and deleted, and the behaviour change the diff does not spell out. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#whole-change-including-unstated
- `change-history-pull`: Retrieve the related pull request and commits while reading a change. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#change-history-pull
- `single-safety-fact-search`: Find the one fact that makes a change safe and clears most risky cases, and spend the time there, not on a long list of possibilities. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#single-safety-fact-search
- `dependency-source-and-pin`: Read the called library's source and confirm its pinned version and whether it is locally patched. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#dependency-source-and-pin
- `timing-and-lifecycle-analysis`: Work out when things execute, including deferred callbacks, teardown and framework differences. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#timing-and-lifecycle-analysis
- `non-symbol-coupling-trace`: Follow links symbol search misses: returned data shapes, database columns, wire formats, another language reading the same bytes, feature flags and code several hops away. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#non-symbol-coupling-trace
- `likelihood-and-cost-per-risk`: Give each risk an honest probability and an honest cost. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#likelihood-and-cost-per-risk
- `confirmed-and-cleared-split`: Keep confirmed risks apart from those checked and cleared, saying why each cleared one is fine. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#confirmed-and-cleared-split
- `empty-search-is-finding`: Count a search that returned nothing as a result to report, not as work to discard. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#empty-search-is-finding
- `no-fabrication`: Never fabricate citations, data or examples. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `multi-model-question-on-wide-change`: For a big or wide change, put the same question to more than one model and merge the answers. — reject
- `handback-what-it-does`: Say what changed, including the non-obvious part. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#handback-what-it-does
- `handback-safety-fact-with-grade`: State the safety fact, its ladder level and its proof, or mark it unproven. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#handback-safety-fact-with-grade
- `handback-risk-fields`: For each risk give how it breaks, the actual file and line, likelihood and severity, how to check it, and the proof for those that matter. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#handback-risk-fields
- `handback-pre-merge-check`: Give the cheapest test or reproduction able to expose the actual bug, along with any script written. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → review#handback-pre-merge-check
- `secret-containment`: Keep secrets and private data out of any destination not authorized to hold them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

#### core · Verification · Review — skill:pstack/skills/interrogate
- `break-it-mandate`: Assign adversaries to try to break a change or design rather than assess it in general. — adopt → interrogate#break-it-mandate
- `run-proven-finding`: Let a finding stand only when a run executed in the review shows it, so a claim nobody ran is no finding. — adopt → interrogate#run-proven-finding
- `inspection-only-authority`: Treat a review or analysis request as authority to inspect and report only, never to change the work. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `named-scope-first`: Use the scope the user names when one is given. — adopt → interrogate#named-scope-first
- `merge-base-through-tree-scope`: When no scope is named, review the branch from where it left the base branch up to and including the working tree. — defer
- `intent-restated-first`: Restate the change's intent in your own words before sending out adversaries. — adopt → interrogate#intent-restated-first
- `intent-from-request-commits-pr`: Derive the intent from the request, the commits and the pull request description. — adopt → interrogate#intent-from-stated-sources
- `ask-when-intent-unclear`: Ask the user when the intent cannot be established. — adopt → interrogate#ask-or-not-run-on-intent
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state. — adopt → interrogate#own-output-location
- `one-message-fan-out`: Launch every candidate or adversary in one message as background subagents. — reject
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout. — adopt → interrogate#dropout-proceeds-noted
- `uncommitted-changes-seeded`: Seed every adversary workspace with the uncommitted work included in the review scope. — adopt → interrogate#verified-snapshot-copy
- `general-purpose-adversary`: Spawn each adversary as the general-purpose subagent type. — reject
- `adversary-fixed-brief`: Hand every adversary the scope, the intent and one unchanging instruction to break the work, replacing the usual task and rationale request. — adopt → interrogate#adversaries-by-model-or-angle
- `run-against-real-code`: Require each finding to be demonstrated by executing something against the actual code, such as a failing test, a reproduction script or revealing command output. — adopt → interrogate#run-against-real-code
- `design-proof-by-probe`: For a design or plan, prove a finding by running a prototype or probing the current tree. — adopt → interrogate#design-proof-by-probe
- `repros-stay-in-copy`: Keep each adversary's reproduction material inside its own output location. — adopt → interrogate#repros-stay-in-copy
- `finding-repro-report`: Require each finding to carry a title, the exact command, the printed output and the output the intent requires. — adopt → interrogate#finding-repro-report
- `style-findings-excluded`: Leave style, naming and structure out of an adversary's findings. — reject
- `future-change-risk-excluded`: Leave out hazards that matter only after a future change. — reject
- `no-findings-valid`: Accept a report with no findings as a valid result, and say so explicitly when none remain. — adopt → interrogate#no-findings-valid
- `coordinator-replays-finding`: Have the coordinator verify each finding by running its command again. — adopt → interrogate#coordinator-replays-finding
- `reproduced-and-breaks-intent`: Keep a finding only if the output shows the failure and that failure breaks the stated intent. — adopt → interrogate#reproduced-and-breaks-intent
- `drop-unverified-findings`: Remove every finding that fails the keep test. — adopt → interrogate#three-replay-outcomes
- `merge-by-root-cause`: Combine findings that share one root cause. — adopt → interrogate#merge-by-root-cause
- `no-judge-pick-or-graft`: Omit judging, base selection and grafting from a review by adversaries. — reject
- `union-of-verified-findings`: Keep every verified finding across adversaries rather than selecting one adversary's list. — adopt → interrogate#union-of-verified-findings
- `output-opens-with-intent`: Open the output with the intent restatement. — adopt → interrogate#output-opens-with-intent
- `output-finding-fields`: For each verified finding, report its command, its output and how it breaks the intent. — adopt → interrogate#output-finding-fields
- `adversary-attribution`: Name the adversaries that found each verified finding. — adopt → interrogate#adversary-attribution
- `dropped-finding-accounting`: Report for each adversary how many findings were dropped and why. — adopt → interrogate#dropped-finding-accounting

#### core · Verification · Review — skill:pstack/skills/no-comments
- `merge-base-through-tree-scope`: When no scope is named, review the branch from where it left the base branch up to and including the working tree. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#merge-base-through-tree-scope
- `named-scope-first`: Use the scope the user names when one is given. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#named-scope-first
- `comment-critic-role`: Spawn a fixed subagent role to audit comments and pass it the scope. — reject
- `defer-to-fresh-critic`: Give weight to a critic's fresh perspective over the caller's own attachment. — reject
- `role-rules-not-restated`: Do not repeat a spawned role's rules in the request that spawns it. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `read-worker-output`: Open the diff or artifact a worker produced and hold it to the evidence its brief named, instead of relying on its summary. — reject
- `critic-out-of-bounds-refused`: Refuse a critic's edits to application code and any of its work outside the given scope. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#comment-pass-stays-in-bounds
- `comment-exception-gate`: Refuse deleting a comment a stated exception protects, and bring one back only with that exact exception and proof within scope. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-no-comments#exact-proof-settles-a-protected-keep
- `misstated-kill-reason-refused`: Refuse a report whose reason for a mandatory comment deletion is wrong. — reject
- `kept-code-not-guilty`: Refuse flags that treat intentionally retained code as being at fault. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#kept-code-not-guilty
- `reshape-flags-stay-open`: Keep flags asking to restructure surprising first-party code open, without bringing their comments back. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#reshape-flags-open-apart-from-comment
- `comment-keep-needs-proof`: Let a comment survive only with proof it concerns something the team cannot alter. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-no-comments#unsure-comment-kept-and-flagged
- `missed-suppression-audit`: Check the scope for lint and type-checker suppression comments the critic overlooked. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#suppressions-in-comment-sweep
- `safety-suppressions-removed`: Treat suppressions bearing on correctness or safety as findings that must be removed. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-no-comments#safety-suppressions-removed
- `thin-importance-comment-check`: Before accepting a thinly justified decision on a comment marked important, investigate its symbol's behaviour and history. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#thin-importance-comment-check
- `ambiguous-comment-deleted`: Leave an ambiguous deletion deleted, and delete a kept comment that is refuted or stays ambiguous. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-no-comments#unsure-comment-kept-and-flagged
- `one-named-rerun-then-fail`: After rejecting a report, revert it and rerun the critic once with the failure named, and fail the run if the second report is rejected too. — reject
- `trivial-flag-direct-fix`: Resolve simple accepted flags at once through edits such as removing an unused path or parameter, or calling the genuine interface. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#trivial-flag-direct-fix
- `one-sketch-for-accepted-set`: When a fix needs a design, run one design pass over all accepted flags and nearby code, stopping at the sketch and leaving implementation to a later step. — reject
- `smallest-in-scope-root-cause-fix`: Implement the smallest in-scope fix for the underlying cause, and when the cause lies beyond scope land that fix and list the rest as open. — reject
- `named-workarounds-removed`: Eliminate every workaround the findings name. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#named-workarounds-removed
- `principles-never-widen-scope`: Treat guiding principles as intent only, never permission to expand the boundary or fix other instances. — reject
- `no-symptom-guards`: Never add a guard that merely masks a symptom. — reject
- `constraint-comment-class`: Treat comments that forbid removal, forbid rewording or require consulting someone as a distinct class. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-no-comments#constraint-comment-class
- `unchangeable-constraint-kept`: Leave kept comments that concern things outside the team's control. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-no-comments#unchangeable-constraint-kept
- `cheapest-enforcement-offer`: For other constraint comments, propose the least costly enforcement available in scope, whether a type, runtime check, test or CI lint. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#cheapest-enforcement-offer
- `encoding-approval-gate`: Apply an encoding only with approval, through the route the caller names or given by the caller in advance. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#encoding-approval-gate
- `encode-then-delete`: When an encoding is approved, add the enforcement and then remove the comment. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#encode-then-delete
- `unencoded-constraint-reported`: Without approval, delete the comment, report the constraint as open and sketch any out-of-scope work. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#unencoded-constraint-kept-and-reported
- `comment-audit-report`: Report the counts of comments deleted and restored, reruns, the sketch, fixes, encodings offered and done, constraints left unenforced and open items. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → no-comments#comment-sweep-report

#### core · Verification · Validation — skill:pstack/skills/principle-prove-it-works
- `direct-observation`: Verify a result by observing the real thing (run it, read the actual value, check liveness directly), never a proxy, a cached view or a self-report. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `suspect-the-observation`: When a check fails unexpectedly, test the observation method before concluding the system is wrong. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `scripted-proof`: Prefer a deterministic, rerunnable script as the proof of a result, and keep its output for a reviewer. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `audit-trail-proof-commit`: Keep a proof artifact visible to the human, and commit it only when large or complex work needs an auditable trail. — adopt → build-a-lever#proposed-artifact-commit

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:pstack/skills/correct
- `recurring-lesson-to-check`: When a correction or instruction recurs, encode it as a lint, flag, runtime check or script instead of adding more instruction text. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `next-agent-test`: Prefer a design where an edit that looks right from one file is right everywhere, assuming the next editor sees only the files it opened and copies the nearest example. — reject
- `mine-and-group-mistakes`: Collect mistakes from recent history, reverts, review remarks, instruction files and workaround comments, and cluster them into classes. — defer
- `two-occurrence-threshold`: Count a class of mistake only after it has happened at least twice. — defer
- `fix-at-highest-level`: Try fixes for a repeated mistake in order of architecture, types, lint or CI, tests and finally docs, stopping at the highest level that works. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → authoring-for-agents#fix-at-highest-level
- `split-ownership-flag`: Give each piece of state one owner, so that others read it or ask the owner to change it, with no second writer and no copy. — reject
- `one-way-per-task`: Keep a single way to do a task, moving callers off the others and deleting them in the same change. — reject
- `unreachable-internals`: Make a module's internals unreachable, so that an import from outside fails the build. — reject
- `derived-or-checked-lists`: Derive duplicate lists from one, or make the build fail when lists that cannot be derived disagree. — reject
- `delete-copyable-old-ways`: Remove outdated approaches and dead code an agent might imitate. — reject
- `unrepresentable-invalid-states`: Shape types so the checker rejects impossible states, defining special cases out of existence instead of handling them. — reject
- `check-error-names-replacement`: Where wrong code can still compile, add a check whose message points at the specific file, type or function to use. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → authoring-for-agents#check-error-names-replacement
- `ratchet-on-common-patterns`: When a pattern is already widespread, fail only on changes that add more of it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → authoring-for-agents#ratchet-on-common-patterns
- `green-on-break-test-fixed`: Repair or remove a test that stays green when its behaviour breaks. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#green-on-break-test-fixed
- `implementation-test-deletion`: When internals change, rewrite or delete tests that only protect the old implementation, asserting the current contract instead. — reject
- `build-check-over-rule`: Default to building a deterministic check over writing a prose rule for any mechanical finding. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#build-check-over-rule
- `most-frequent-classes-first`: Fix the classes of mistake that occur most often in this pass. — defer
- `small-single-purpose-commits`: Keep each commit small and about one thing. — reject
- `check-proved-on-real-mistake`: Show each new check failing against a mistake that actually occurred. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → authoring-for-agents#check-proved-on-real-mistake
- `same-command-local-and-ci`: Run the identical command on a developer machine and in CI. — defer
- `inline-exception-with-reason`: Record an exception to a check on the offending line along with its justification. — defer
- `expiring-exceptions`: Give every exception to a check an expiry date. — defer
- `human-approved-exceptions`: Require a person's approval for each exception to a check. — defer
- `rule-to-enforcer-table`: Maintain in the agent instruction file a table pairing each rule with what enforces it. — reject
- `correction-adds-rule`: On each operator correction, fix the mistake and also add the rule. — reject
- `unenforced-repeat-escalation`: If a corrected rule already existed without enforcement, count it as a repeat and solve it at the top workable level within that change. — reject
- `structural-fix-only`: Once a rule is enforced by structure, delete the instruction that restated it. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#check-pointer-not-restatement
- `class-evidence-level-report`: Report for every class of mistake the supporting evidence, the chosen level and why no higher level worked. — defer

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:pstack/skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
- `recurring-lesson-to-check`: When a correction or instruction recurs, encode it as a lint, flag, runtime check or script instead of adding more instruction text. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

- `repitch-trigger`: When a message did not land, stop and re-pitch it rather than adding more. — adopt → brief-me#repitch-trigger

#### core · X · Communication — skill:pstack/skills/unslop
- `meaning-and-tone-preserved`: Keep the original sense of a text and fit its intended tone when editing it. — adopt → unslop#meaning-preserved-edit
- `ing-phrase-cut`: Delete tacked-on present-participle phrases that claim significance, or back them with real sources. — adopt → unslop#ing-phrase-cut
- `vague-attribution-cut`: Name the source of any claim credited to unnamed groups, or delete the claim. — adopt → unslop#vague-attribution-cut
- `tell-vocabulary-swap`: Replace a fixed list of overused elevated words with plain ones. — adopt → unslop#tell-vocabulary-swap
- `plain-is-has`: Use is or has in place of grand verbs standing in for them. — adopt → unslop#plain-is-has
- `not-just-but-cut`: Replace the construction that denies one thing to promote another with a direct statement of the point. — adopt → unslop#not-just-but-cut
- `forced-triplet-cut`: List as many items as naturally exist, never forcing a group of three. — adopt → unslop#forced-triplet-cut
- `synonym-cycling-cut`: Keep one term for one referent instead of rotating through synonyms. — adopt → unslop#synonym-cycling-cut
- `false-range-cut`: Replace a from-to construction that has no real scale with a direct list. — adopt → unslop#false-range-cut
- `em-dash-ban`: Ban em dashes and their substitutes, including parentheses, en dashes and hyphens as dashes, leaving only periods and commas to separate thoughts. — adopt → unslop#no-em-dash
- `mid-sentence-colon-cut`: Keep colons for lists and examples, rewriting mid-sentence uses and the comparison framing around them. — adopt → unslop#mid-sentence-colon-cut
- `bold-restraint`: Do not bold every proper noun or acronym. — adopt → unslop#bold-restraint
- `inline-header-list-convert`: Turn bullets whose bold label merely restates the line into prose, keeping a period-ended label followed by new detail. — adopt → unslop#inline-header-list-convert
- `sentence-case-headings`: Write headings in sentence case. — adopt → unslop#sentence-case-headings
- `no-decorative-emoji`: Remove ornamental emoji from headings and bullets. — adopt → unslop#no-decorative-emoji
- `straight-quotes`: Replace typographic quotation marks with straight ones. — adopt → unslop#straight-quotes
- `chatbot-phrase-cut`: Remove assistant pleasantries, offers of further help and excited discovery lines. — adopt → unslop#chatbot-phrase-cut
- `sycophancy-cut`: Remove praise and agreement openers and answer directly. — adopt → unslop#sycophancy-cut
- `filler-phrase-cut`: Shorten wordy stock phrases and delete empty announcements of importance. — adopt → unslop#filler-phrase-cut
- `hedge-stack-trim`: Reduce piled-up qualifiers to a single modal. — adopt → unslop#hedge-stack-trim
- `generic-conclusion-cut`: Replace optimistic sign-offs with specific plans or facts. — adopt → unslop#generic-conclusion-cut
- `metaphor-noun-swap`: Replace a listed set of pseudo-technical figurative nouns with their concrete equivalents. — adopt → unslop#local-metaphor-noun-swap
- `name-the-mechanism`: Rewrite a sentence that conveys an impression so that it states a mechanism or number, cutting it if it cannot become an instruction, fact or figure. — adopt → unslop#name-the-mechanism
- `portable-sentence-cut`: Cut a sentence that would fit another project's docs unchanged. — reject
- `dense-sentence-split`: Split or trim any sentence the reader must reread to parse. — adopt → unslop#dense-sentence-split
- `active-voice`: Name the actor in place of a passive, keeping passive only when the actor is unknown or does not matter. — adopt → unslop#active-voice
- `adverb-cut`: Cut an adverb, using a stronger verb or the measured figure in its place. — adopt → unslop#adverb-cut
- `plain-word`: Use the common word over a fancier synonym. — adopt → unslop#plain-word
- `mannered-prose-cut`: Replace aphorisms, rhetorical fragments, personified code, figurative verbs and stock framing with literal phrasing. — adopt → unslop#mannered-prose-cut
- `over-compression-fix`: Restore articles, verbs and whole sentences, and spell out arrows, symbols and abbreviations. — adopt → unslop#over-compression-fix
- `stable-rule-numbers`: Keep rule numbers as permanent identifiers that other documents can cite, leaving a deleted rule's number unused. — reject

#### core · X · Continuity — skill:pstack/skills/recall
- `current-state-capsule-goal`: Rebuild recent working context into a compact statement of the present position and what comes next. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#current-state-capsule-goal
- `scoped-reading`: Search narrowly and read only the context the task needs, widening when dependencies or uncertainty call for it and never bulk-reading. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

- `skip-mining-with-supplied-state`: If the user already gave paths, branch and the change, use that and do no mining. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#skip-mining-with-supplied-state

- `cheap-model-fan-out`: Spawn concurrent subagents on a fast, inexpensive model, each covering a slice of the chat history. — reject
- `order-by-real-mtime`: Sort candidates by actual modification time, never by identifier name. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#order-by-real-mtime
- `grep-then-read-matching-regions`: Search for the topic first, then open only chats that match and only the parts of them that bear on it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#grep-then-read-matching-regions
- `exclude-current-and-noise-chats`: Leave out the current chat along with subagent, evaluation and test chats. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#exclude-current-and-noise-chats
- `uniform-per-chat-schema`: Require from each subagent one block per chat recording topic, goal, decisions, unresolved threads, difficulties, corrections and produced artifacts. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#uniform-per-chat-schema
- `finding-cited-by-source-kind`: Cite chat findings by chat identifier and shared-record findings by pull request, ticket, permalink or error-tracker issue. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#finding-cited-by-source-kind
- `direct-search-for-small-corpus`: With one or two chats, search directly without fanning out. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#direct-search-for-small-corpus
- `bulk-to-subagents`: Send bulk reading and large outputs to subagents and keep only their summaries in the main thread. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `default-shared-record-sweep`: Search the shared record by default when a feature, file, subsystem, area or bug is named, omitting it only for activity recall with no named target. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#default-shared-record-sweep
- `one-investigator-per-source`: Hand a shared-record sweep to existing per-source investigators, one for each source. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#one-helper-per-sizeable-source
- `retarget-investigator-question`: Change the investigators' question from design rationale to current state, failed attempts and ongoing user reports. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#retarget-investigator-question
- `sweep-parallel-to-mining`: Run the shared-record sweep at the same time as chat-history mining. — reject
- `empty-search-is-finding`: Count a search that returned nothing as a result to report, not as work to discard. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#empty-search-is-finding
- `unreachable-data-is-gap`: Report data you could not reach, through a missing tool, denied access, retention or deletion, as a coverage gap and never as a null result. — reject
- `primary-evidence-check`: Check consequential claims from summaries, memory and agent reports against primary evidence before relying on them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `full-transcript-for-agent-behaviour`: When the answer depends on what an agent actually did, read the complete transcript and not a trimmed local copy. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#full-transcript-for-agent-behaviour
- `brief-grouped-by-thread`: Organize a recall brief by thread and stay on the named topic. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#brief-grouped-by-thread
- `brief-section-order`: Present capsule, thread status, problems and next move in that order, with further detail below or cut. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#brief-section-order
- `capped-capsule-section`: Hold the opening capsule to five bullets at most. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#capped-capsule-section
- `status-tagged-thread-lines`: Give each thread one line with exactly one tag from merged, open pull request, in flight, verified uncommitted, reverted or planned. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#status-tagged-thread-lines-with-abandoned
- `capped-recurring-problems`: List at most five recurring problems, including persistent user symptoms and reverted fixes, so the next try starts from the last failure. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#capped-recurring-problems
- `single-next-move`: End with the one most useful concrete next action. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#single-next-move
- `adjacent-excluded-unless-blocking`: Leave out a neighbouring feature or ticket unless it blocks this one. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#adjacent-excluded-unless-blocking
- `cut-detail-before-threads`: When a recall brief passes a screen, remove detail ahead of removing threads. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#cut-detail-before-threads
- `secret-containment`: Keep secrets and private data out of any destination not authorized to hold them. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `reply-is-the-deliverable`: Return the deliverable itself as the reply, never an account of what was done to produce it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → recall#reply-is-the-deliverable

#### core · X · Continuity — skill:pstack/skills/show-me-your-work
- `single-tsv-decision-log`: Keep one authoritative decision log as a single TSV file with one single-line row per decision. — adopt → decision-trail#single-tsv-decision-log
- `evidence-pointer-cell`: Make a row's evidence cell a resolvable pointer such as a commit, pull request, file and line or artifact path, never narrative. — adopt → decision-trail#evidence-pointer-cell
- `trail-header-template`: Start a new log from a supplied file holding only the header row. — reject
- `trail-six-columns`: Give every row the fixed columns ts in ISO8601, phase or workstream, the decision in one line, why, evidence, and result as an outcome or state. — adopt → decision-trail#trail-six-columns
- `trail-sample-rows`: Show a sample log in the expected plain style. — reject
- `plain-row-wording`: Write rows the way you would tell a colleague, in concrete words, spelling a guiding principle out in place of citing it as a tag. — adopt → decision-trail#plain-row-wording
- `positional-row-helper`: Append rows through a script that takes the log path and exactly five positional cell values, printing usage and failing on any other count. — adopt → decision-trail#named-cell-row-helper
- `hand-append-caveat`: Allow a row appended by hand, giving cells from generated or user-supplied text the helper's byte-level care. — reject
- `decision-points-only`: Log decision points and checkpoints (a chosen fork, a finished unit with its verification, a pivot or revert with its cause, a surfaced blocker, a fixed gate), never each action or a self-evident step. — adopt → decision-trail#decision-points-only
- `row-per-iteration`: Have a looping run write one row for each iteration. — adopt → decision-trail#row-per-iteration
- `helper-aborts-on-failure`: Have the log helper abort on any command failure, unset variable or pipeline failure. — reject
- `creates-log-parent`: Have the log helper create a missing parent directory. — adopt → decision-trail#creates-log-parent
- `header-on-empty-file`: Have the log helper write the header row when the log is missing or empty. — adopt → decision-trail#locked-single-header
- `append-mode-writes`: Write the header and rows only in append mode, so a false empty-file test costs a stray header and never the rows. — adopt → decision-trail#append-mode-writes
- `automatic-utc-stamp`: Have the log helper stamp each row with the current UTC time so the caller supplies none. — adopt → decision-trail#automatic-utc-stamp
- `cell-whitespace-strip`: Replace tabs, newlines and carriage returns in each cell with spaces. — adopt → decision-trail#cell-whitespace-strip
- `formula-cell-quote`: Prefix a single quote to any cell starting with a character a spreadsheet parses as a formula, so hostile text cannot execute when the log is opened. — adopt → decision-trail#numeric-safe-formula-quote
- `run-boundary`: Count one agent conversation with its later turns and summaries as one run, and a pickup, replacement agent or new chat as a new one. — adopt → decision-trail#run-boundary
- `start-row-triggers`: Have a run adding to a log with rows write a `start` row first, and on returning read the log's tail and write a fresh one if another run's `start` has appeared. — adopt → decision-trail#start-row-triggers
- `start-row-contents`: Have a `start` row name the timestamp range of the rows this run did not write and identify this run in its evidence, using the `start` phase for nothing else. — adopt → decision-trail#start-row-contents
- `local-log-default`: Keep the log as an uncommitted working file at a fixed name in the work directory, or under a hidden audit folder by task slug when several efforts run at once. — adopt → decision-trail#trail-location-rule
- `commit-on-reviewer-need`: Leave the log out of Git unless the work is large enough that a reviewer could not trust the outcome without it. — adopt → decision-trail#proposed-trail-commit
- `append-only-supersede`: Never edit or delete a ledger record; correct or reverse one by appending a record that supersedes it. — adopt → decision-trail#append-only-supersede
- `script-evidence-preference`: Favour evidence generated by committed scripts over hand-made one-off evidence. — adopt → decision-trail#script-evidence-preference
- `end-of-run-audit`: Before handing back, check the log for truthfulness against what happened in the run. — adopt → decision-trail#end-of-run-audit
- `transcript-path-audit`: Audit from this run's transcript in the active workspace's transcript directory, whose location the system prompt gives. — reject
- `no-cross-project-transcript-search`: Never search across project transcript folders during an audit, because that exposes unrelated private conversations. — adopt → decision-trail#no-cross-project-transcript-search
- `audit-own-stretches`: Limit an audit to this run's row stretches, each from one of its `start` rows or the log's first row to the next `start` row of another run. — adopt → decision-trail#audit-own-stretches
- `row-maps-to-real-event`: Check that each audited row corresponds to a decision or action that actually occurred. — adopt → decision-trail#verified-record-row-walk
- `evidence-resolves-check`: Check that each audited row's pointer resolves and supports what the row says. — adopt → decision-trail#evidence-resolves-check
- `unlogged-fork-gap`: Treat a fork, pivot or abandoned path that shaped the work with no row as a gap, and add the row in the audit. — adopt → decision-trail#unlogged-fork-gap
- `audit-supersedes-in-place-of-editing`: Have an audit change no row, even an invented one, and add a row superseding it with what really happened and a pointer that resolves. — adopt → decision-trail#audit-supersedes-in-place-of-editing
- `foreign-row-on-own-evidence`: Supersede a row outside the audited stretches only when this run's own work shows it to be wrong. — adopt → decision-trail#foreign-row-on-own-evidence
- `other-family-trail-review`: Before handing back, have a subagent from a different model family review the run, with no self-review in its place. — adopt → decision-trail#same-family-or-unreviewed
- `trail-and-transcript-review`: Give the reviewer the audit trail and the run's transcript as its inputs. — adopt → decision-trail#evidence-pointer-review
- `attention-scan-not-redo`: Have the trail's reviewer look for what is suboptimal or risky for the user's attention and not repeat the work. — adopt → decision-trail#attention-scan-not-redo
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `trail-review-flags`: Have the trail's reviewer flag weak or absent evidence, checks skipped or claimed without proof, choices risky in hindsight, and gaps a casual read would miss. — adopt → decision-trail#trail-review-flags
- `attention-section`: End every reply of a run with a trail in an Attention section, opening with a line naming the reviewer's model and then each flag with its rows or moments, where no flags is allowed and the model name is not optional. — adopt → decision-trail#attention-with-coverage
- `trail-reading-method`: Read a trail from top to bottom, following the evidence pointers and spot-checking. — reject
- `trail-rendering-tips`: Show the log as a table through the forge's TSV view or the `column` command. — reject
- `single-trail-format-owner`: Have other skills needing a trail refer to this one by name and define no trail or columns of their own. — reject

#### core · X · Coordination — skill:pstack/skills/arena
- `phase-todos`: Open a task list with one item per phase before beginning. — reject
- `same-prompt-contract`: Give every candidate the same prompt, which serves as the binding definition of the job. — reject
- `artifact-named-up-front`: State exactly what artifact each candidate must produce before any candidate starts. — adopt → model-council#artifact-named-up-front
- `task-rubric-criteria`: Write three to six concrete, gradeable success criteria specific to this task. — adopt → model-council#task-rubric-criteria
- `rubric-withheld-from-candidates`: Keep the success criteria from the candidates, who see only the task. — adopt → model-council#rubric-withheld-from-candidates
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `rejected-model-swap`: When a spawn refuses a model, use the default and disclose the swap, then the nearest same-family model if the default is refused too. — reject
- `model-family-prefix-map`: Sort models into families by name prefix. — reject
- `unrunnable-seat-dropped`: Remove a seat no valid model can run, and disclose it. — reject
- `seat-backfill-to-minimum`: When dropped seats leave too few runners, add runners up to a floor on a surviving model or the parent's, and disclose the choice. — reject
- `extra-runners-per-direction`: Add candidates when the work must explore several design directions. — reject
- `same-model-for-generation`: Use one model for every seat when output is limited by generation rather than judgment. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `own-output-location`: Give every candidate or adversary a separate output location, so they share no writable state. — adopt → model-council#own-output-location
- `worktree-or-temp-output`: Prefer a git worktree for each candidate's output, falling back to a per-candidate temporary directory. — reject
- `one-message-fan-out`: Launch every candidate or adversary in one message as background subagents. — reject
- `candidate-brief-fields`: Hand each candidate the task, the shared grounding's path and its own output path. — reject
- `rationale-names-rejected`: Have each candidate deliver, with its artifact, a short rationale naming the alternatives it weighed and what it rejected. — adopt → model-council#rationale-names-rejected
- `dropout-proceeds-noted`: Go on with the remaining candidates or adversaries when one produces nothing, and record the dropout. — adopt → model-council#dropout-proceeds-noted
- `judge-after-candidates`: Start the judge only after every candidate has finished. — reject
- `single-judge`: Use exactly one judge for a comparison of candidates. — reject
- `read-only-judge`: Give the judge read-only access. — adopt → model-council#read-only-judge
- `judge-outside-lead-family`: Never let the judge's model share a family with the coordinating agent's model. — adopt → model-council#judge-other-family-or-stated
- `judge-pool-walk`: Choose the judge by trying a pool's entries outside the parent's family in order, skipping parent aliases, moving to a nearby slug or the next entry on refusal and falling back to a default pool. — reject
- `judge-skip-pick-alone`: When no judge can run, skip it, pick the base alone and say so. — reject
- `family-check-unrun-disclosed`: When the coordinator's own model is unknown, try the judge pool in order and disclose that the family check did not run. — adopt → model-council#judge-other-family-or-stated
- `rubric-given-to-judge`: Give the judge the success criteria to score against. — adopt → model-council#rubric-given-to-judge
- `path-labelled-candidates`: Show the judge each candidate under its path label. — adopt → model-council#path-labelled-candidates
- `judge-criterion-scores`: Have the judge score each candidate on each criterion. — adopt → model-council#judge-criterion-scores
- `judge-recommends-base`: Have the judge recommend a base and justify the recommendation. — adopt → model-council#judge-recommends-base
- `judge-parallel-with-picker`: Run the judge while the picker reads, not before or after. — reject
- `full-read-before-pick`: Read every candidate in full before choosing a base. — adopt → model-council#full-read-before-pick
- `picker-criterion-scores`: Score each candidate on each criterion instead of by overall impression. — adopt → model-council#picker-criterion-scores
- `pick-compared-with-judge`: Compare your scored pick with the judge's, treating the same choice as confirmation. — adopt → model-council#pick-compared-with-judge
- `disagreement-rereads-rationales`: Treat a disagreement with the judge as a sign of bias or an unclear rubric, and read both rationales before deciding. — adopt → model-council#disagreement-rereads-rationales
- `base-chosen-for-extensibility`: Choose the base a later maintainer could extend most easily while keeping invariants intact. — adopt → model-council#base-chosen-for-extensibility
- `near-tie-smaller-surface`: Break a near-tie in favour of the cleaner boundary or the smaller interface. — adopt → model-council#near-tie-smaller-surface
- `loser-graft-pass`: Go through each losing candidate once more for parts worth carrying over. — adopt → model-council#loser-graft-pass
- `sparse-grafts`: Expect only one or two grafts from a losing candidate, not the bulk of it. — adopt → model-council#sparse-grafts
- `hand-folded-grafts`: Rewrite each graft into the base by hand, so the result keeps one coherent design rather than pasted fragments. — adopt → model-council#hand-folded-grafts
- `converged-shape-no-graft`: When candidates reach one shape, record the agreement and ship that shape with no graft. — adopt → model-council#converged-shape-no-graft
- `divergence-reframes`: When candidates differ wildly, treat the frame as too loose, then reframe and rerun instead of blending them. — adopt → model-council#divergence-reframes-once
- `synthesized-artifact-verified`: Verify the merged artifact to the same standard as any other output. — adopt → model-council#graft-change-rerun
- `verify-miss-routes-back`: Send a verification problem back to reframing or to grafting, whichever caused it, and never hide it. — adopt → model-council#verify-miss-returns-once
- `single-synthesized-artifact`: End with one merged artifact rather than a set of alternatives. — adopt → model-council#single-synthesized-artifact
- `synthesis-decision-record`: Record the chosen base candidate with its reason, what was grafted from the rest and why each was rejected. — adopt → model-council#synthesis-decision-record
- `note-judge-status`: Record in the synthesis note the judge's verdict or that the judge was skipped. — adopt → model-council#note-judge-status
- `note-convergence-dropouts`: Record any convergence or dropped candidates in the synthesis note. — adopt → model-council#note-convergence-dropouts
- `note-verification-result`: Record the verification result in the synthesis note. — adopt → model-council#note-verification-result

#### core · X · Coordination — skill:pstack/skills/figure-it-out

- `framing-before-run`: Do the grounding before starting, and do not begin a run until its framing can be stated. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md

- `rigor-biased-high-by-reversibility`: Pick a rigor level biased high, raised for one-way doors and wide impact and lowered for reversible low-stakes steps. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `rigor-means-gates-and-artifacts`: Define rigor as concrete gates and artifacts, not extra effort. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `framing-and-tradeoffs-shown`: Show the human the framing and its tradeoffs ahead of a long run. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `reversible-work-proceeds`: Proceed without asking on reversible work, then present the result and its reasoning so the human can correct it afterwards, leaving product direction to the human. — reject
- `single-checkpoint-on-long-run`: Give a multi-hour run one checkpoint with the human. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `independently-landable-units`: Split the work into atomic units that can each land independently. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `riskiest-unknown-first`: Order the units so the largest unknown is tackled first. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `scaffold-first`: Sequence first the work every later phase benefits from (CI, linting, test infrastructure, shared types) before features. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `harness-with-pre-change-baseline`: Build the verification harness first and capture a baseline before changing anything, so results read as old against new. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `design-contest-on-one-way-doors`: For design choices that cannot be undone, run a design skill that pits alternatives against each other, and skip that for mechanical work or a settled design. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `fan-out-across-seams-only`: Decide what runs in parallel, parallelizing only where the work has seams and not over-fanning. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `worktree-or-branch-per-worker`: Give each parallel worker its own worktree or branch. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `written-phase-list-for-review`: Write down the designed phases as the thing the human reviews. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `designed-steps-as-todos`: Insert the designed steps as concrete todo items between the loop and audit entries. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `rolling-log-rows`: Add a trail row as each step lands, not all at the end. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `hypothesis-per-unit`: Treat each unit as an experiment with a stated hypothesis. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md

- `keep-or-revert-on-predicate`: Keep a change that moved things forward and revert one that did not. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `verified-unit-sequence`: Split multi-step work into small units that each end in a checked state, and start the next only when the current one passes. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `direct-observation`: Verify a result by observing the real thing (run it, read the actual value, check liveness directly), never a proxy, a cached view or a self-report. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

- `fix-wrong-gate-separately`: When the gate itself is wrong, correct it in its own change and do not route around it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `three-value-verdict`: Report results as verified, not verified or inconclusive, with inconclusive never counting as a pass. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `no-hidden-negatives`: Do not conceal negative results. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
- `commit-on-reviewer-need`: Leave the log out of Git unless the work is large enough that a reviewer could not trust the outcome without it. — adopt → decision-trail#proposed-trail-commit

- `designed-run-reply-fields`: Reply with the designed playbook, rigor level and reason, trail path, what is verified against the predicate and what is open. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/figure-it-out.md
