- `lead-with-what-matters`: Open an explanation on its central point and on what matters most to this reader. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#lead-with-what-matters
- `confidence-language-kept`: Keep the tier words and hedges that mark uncertainty when editing a finished answer. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#confidence-language-kept
- `pick-few-takeaways`: Choose a small number of things the person should come away understanding before explaining anything. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#pick-few-takeaways
- `learner-context-from-conversation`: Work out why the person is asking and what they already know from the conversation, not by questioning them. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#learner-context-from-conversation
- `depth-where-asked`: Omit what the person evidently already knows and spend the depth on the area they asked about. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#depth-where-asked
- `orient-then-use-investigation`: Read a body of work only far enough to get oriented, and take the digging from a dedicated investigation rather than redoing it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#orient-then-use-investigation
- `parallel-investigations-combined`: Run the how and why investigations at the same time and merge what they return. — reject
- `investigation-sized-to-question`: Run both investigations for a subsystem and possibly only one for a small change. — reject
- `narrow-rationale-search`: Keep a slow rationale search narrow by default through the question it is given, so it records what it skipped, widening only when the reasoning is the point. — reject
- `plain-definition-first`: Begin by naming the thing and defining it in general terms, using its common name if one exists. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#plain-definition-first
- `general-tied-to-local-case`: After the general definition, connect it to how this codebase uses the idea. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#general-tied-to-local-case
- `build-up-order`: Proceed from definition to mechanism, then deeper reasons, then edge cases. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#build-up-order
- `problem-and-mechanism-per-part`: For each part, explain the problem it addresses and how it actually operates. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#problem-and-mechanism-per-part
- `walkthrough-of-user-action`: When it helps the idea land, trace what happens step by step as someone performs the action. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#walkthrough-of-user-action
- `no-symbol-inventory`: Do not substitute a list of functions and constants for an explanation. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#no-symbol-inventory
- `no-labels-or-step-words`: Print no stock labels announcing the key idea, and never echo a skill's step wording as headers or phrases. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#no-labels-or-step-words
- `smallest-complete-answer-first`: Give a complete answer of one or two sentences first, then stop, adding layers only when asked and never delivering an unbroken block. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#requested-depth-first-answer
- `offer-depth-follow-lead`: Invite the person to go deeper or change topic, and let them steer. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#offer-depth-follow-lead
- `no-quizzes`: Do not test the person or ask them to repeat the idea back. — reject
- `no-teaching-theatre`: Do not announce pauses, sentences to master, or that a part is hard or important; state it, and actually stop when a pause is wanted. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#no-teaching-theatre
- `one-shot-delivery-mode`: When the caller asks for full delivery, give the whole explanation in one reply and place any offer of more depth at the end. — defer
- `show-the-real-artifact`: Bring up the actual diff, source or debugger when that conveys the point most quickly. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#show-the-real-artifact
- `figure-when-faster`: Add a figure when a picture would land faster than prose, and omit one for a single simple point. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#figure-when-faster
- `incremental-diagram-series`: For three or more moving parts, draw a sequence in which each figure repeats the last and adds exactly one part, and never rely on one complete figure, of whatever kind. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#incremental-diagram-series
- `figure-kind-by-idea`: Choose the figure type by the nature of the idea, using a labelled diagram where the labels carry the meaning. — reject
- `complementary-figures`: Use more than one kind of figure when each shows something the other cannot. — defer
- `generated-image-for-spatial-ideas`: For spatial ideas, actually generate a marker-on-whiteboard image with an image tool, with few short labels, instead of describing the picture. — reject
- `plain-colleague-voice`: Write in plain spoken English as if to a coworker, removing filler and hedging while keeping the piece that makes the idea click. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#plain-colleague-voice
- `mechanism-not-metaphor`: State the actual mechanism, never a metaphor, framing or preview of what comes next. — reject
- `density-exemplar`: Supply a worked sample sentence pair that fixes the wanted information density. — reject
- `sentence-case-prose`: Use normal sentence capitalization in prose. — reject
- `no-em-dash`: Use no em dashes, ending the sentence or using a comma or parentheses to separate a thought. — reject
- `comma-budget`: Favour periods, allow at most two commas per sentence, and break a sentence up when clauses accumulate. — reject
- `synonym-cycling-cut`: Keep one term for one referent instead of rotating through synonyms. — reject
- `no-mirror-or-tidy-closer`: Avoid symmetrical constructions and neat concluding lines. — reject
- `reply-is-the-deliverable`: Return the deliverable itself as the reply, never an account of what was done to produce it. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#reply-is-the-deliverable
- `threads-to-chase`: Include the lines of inquiry worth pursuing further. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → teach#threads-to-chase

#### engineering · Discovery · Research — skill:pstack/skills/how
- `stated-scope-reading`: State your reading of an ambiguous target and proceed, so the user can redirect afterward. — adopt → how#immaterial-ambiguity-reading
- `size-gated-explorers`: Answer a narrow question in one pass and split a wide one into angles for separate explorers, merging their findings into one account. — adopt → how#angles-when-wide
- `doubt-takes-simple-path`: Resolve an uncertain size call to the cheaper one-pass path. — reject
- `explanation-sections`: Structure an explanation as overview, concepts, flow, file map and pitfalls, dropping any section that does not apply. — adopt → how#explanation-sections
- `cited-flow-walkthrough`: Walk the flow in prose from trigger to result, naming the files and functions at each step. — adopt → how#cited-flow-walkthrough
- `reconcile-by-reading`: Settle conflicting findings by reading the code itself. — adopt → how#reconcile-by-reading
- `fresh-synthesizer`: Wait for every finding, then have one agent that did no searching weigh the raw findings and write the only answer. — reject
- `light-edit-delivery`: Pass the writer's text on with only light edits for clarity or context, never a substantial rewrite. — reject
- `targeted-gap-check`: Let the writer read the code to confirm a detail or fill a gap without redoing the exploration. — reject
- `flow-diagram-when-clarifying`: Add a flow diagram only for a structured flow across several components, omitting it when prose suffices. — reject
- `real-code-names`: Use real names from the actual code, never invented placeholders. — reject
- `complexity-cause-stated`: When something is hard, give the reason for the difficulty and do not merely describe it. — reject
- `onboarding-altitude`: Pitch an explanation so an experienced engineer new to the area gains a working mental model, short of line-by-line commentary. — reject
- `open-questions-visible`: Carry every gap and open question from the search into the final explanation. — reject
- `assigned-slice-depth`: Give each searching helper one assigned slice to go deep on, telling it that peers cover the rest. — reject
- `explorer-report-template`: Have each explorer report a component inventory, an ordered step trace, the files it read, the boundaries and the non-obvious behaviour. — reject
- `read-only-helper-spawn`: Spawn every exploring helper with enforced read-only access. — reject
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `rejected-model-swap`: When a spawn refuses a model, use the default and disclose the swap, then the nearest same-family model if the default is refused too. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject

#### engineering · Discovery · Research — skill:pstack/skills/why
- `stated-scope-reading`: State your reading of an ambiguous target and proceed, so the user can redirect afterward. — adopt → why#immaterial-ambiguity-reading
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `rejected-model-swap`: When a spawn refuses a model, use the default and disclose the swap, then the nearest same-family model if the default is refused too. — reject
- `job-fit-helper-effort`: Choose each helper's thinking depth and speed tier to suit its job. — reject
- `writable-helper-mode`: Spawn helpers in a writable mode because the read-only mode removes the tool access they need. — reject
- `brief-only-read-only`: Tell helpers to write nothing and change no external state even though their mode permits it. — reject
- `question-typing`: Name the target and classify the question as rationale, tradeoff, edge case, external constraint, dead code or history sweep. — reject
- `code-anchor-first`: Before searching, fix the files, lines, symbols and last commits with blame and rename-following log. — adopt → why#code-anchor-first
- `pr-discussion-pull`: For each substantive commit, read the pull request body, linked issues, comments and reviews. — adopt → why#pr-discussion-pull
- `investigator-brief-assembly`: Build each investigator prompt from a template, one source playbook, one shared code anchor and the original question. — reject
- `full-coverage-search`: Run the search of every available source by default, even an unpromising one, aiming for a complete coverage map. — reject
- `sources-consulted-line`: List each source searched, empty or skipped, with the reason. — adopt → why#sources-consulted-line
- `evidence-source-discovery`: Enumerate the enabled tools and assign each to one of seven evidence categories by its primary evidence. — reject
- `evidence-category-fanout`: Run one investigator per evidence source, all in parallel, with source control always included. — adopt → why#local-evidence-sources
- `repo-evidence-inventory`: Look through commits, pull request threads, inline markers, decision records, changelogs, ticket ids, tests and co-changed files for a repository's history. — adopt → why#local-evidence-sources
- `pickaxe-history-search`: Search history for commits whose diffs add, remove or match a string or pattern. — adopt → why#pickaxe-history-search
- `source-control-trust-ranking`: Rate repository history as the most trustworthy source because it ties directly to the code. — reject
- `incident-source-playbook`: When the target looks defensive, add a search of incident records, incident-labelled tickets and incident channels around the date it was added. — defer
- `incident-commit-signals`: Read commit messages about incidents, added guards or a revert followed by re-application as strong signals of motive. — adopt → why#local-evidence-sources
- `category-strength-map`: State which shape of motivation each evidence category reveals and when it is strongest. — reject
- `provable-irrelevance-bar`: Skip a source for irrelevance only on proof, since probable irrelevance does not qualify. — reject
- `trivial-target-inline-exception`: Answer a single-commit target directly when its pull request text answers fully, after confirming every other search would be redundant. — reject
- `fresh-synthesizer`: Wait for every finding, then have one agent that did no searching weigh the raw findings and write the only answer. — reject
- `framework-first-reading`: Have the writer read the whole confidence framework before writing. — reject
- `gather-without-concluding`: Collect the evidence in full before concluding, forming no answer and picking no side while gathering. — adopt → why#gather-without-concluding
- `confidence-language-kept`: Keep the tier words and hedges that mark uncertainty when editing a finished answer. — adopt → unslop#confidence-language-kept
- `constraints-before-change`: When a change follows, turn the findings into preserve, change, avoid and risk lists. — adopt → why#constraints-before-change
- `recency-bias-check`: Trace past the latest commit, which is not authoritative, to the earlier decisions behind the current shape. — adopt → why#recency-bias-check
- `confidence-tiers`: Place each claim in one tier by its evidence, Direct when an author's written words state the reason, Supported when several indirect items converge, Inferred when a reasonable reading has no explicit support, and Speculative when other explanations fit equally well, phrasing the first two confidently with citations, Inferred with hedges and its reasoning chain, and Speculative as a guess. — adopt → why#confidence-tiers
- `adjacent-citation-gate`: Use words asserting cause, intent, achieved effect or a group decision only on Direct or Supported claims, with a specific citation beside them. — adopt → why#adjacent-citation-gate
- `tier-tagged-sections`: Lay out an answer with one section per evidence class and an explicit tier tag on each bullet, omitting an empty section. — reject
- `searched-and-unknown`: Report an unknown with exactly what was searched, where and with which terms. — adopt → why#searched-and-unknown
- `epistemic-wording-bans`: Ban words that imply self-evidence or triviality and statements of personal belief. — reject
- `no-retrofitted-rationale`: Do not impose a tidy justification on messy history or presume the author chose correctly and reason backward. — adopt → why#no-retrofitted-rationale
- `consistency-is-not-intent`: Do not read a repeated pattern as a deliberate choice, since it may be copying. — adopt → why#consistency-is-not-intent
- `absence-is-not-evidence`: Do not read a lack of mention as proof that something was not a concern. — adopt → why#absence-is-not-evidence
- `embedded-hypothesis-check`: Treat a guess inside the question as one candidate to test independently, then confirm or refute it with citations. — adopt → why#embedded-hypothesis-check
- `contradiction-shown`: Show conflicting sources side by side with citations, leaving the call to the user. — adopt → why#contradiction-shown
- `human-followup-pointer`: Name who could answer a gap and could not be asked, or say the question can be dropped. — reject
- `pre-delivery-claim-audit`: Before delivery, check each claim for a citation or demote it, and check that its phrasing matches its tier. — reject
- `code-not-intent-evidence`: Never cite code or a diff as proof of its author's intent. — adopt → why#code-not-intent-evidence
- `empty-gaps-suspicion`: Treat an answer that mentions no gaps as a warning sign. — reject
- `assigned-slice-depth`: Give each searching helper one assigned slice to go deep on, telling it that peers cover the rest. — reject
- `exact-quote-evidence`: Prefer a precise quotation with a location checkable in seconds to a paragraph of paraphrase. — reject
- `wide-then-narrow-search`: Begin a search with a broad sweep and focus on specific items only afterward. — reject
- `read-whole-item`: Open each item found in full, thread or history included, because a preview or a lone message can mislead. — adopt → why#full-record-reading
- `unreachable-data-is-gap`: Report data you could not reach, through a missing tool, denied access, retention or deletion, as a coverage gap and never as a null result. — adopt → why#unreachable-data-is-gap
- `stop-on-auth-failure`: When a source's tool cannot authenticate, stop and report the source as unsearchable, inventing no findings. — reject
- `correlation-needs-neighbor-check`: Treat a before-and-after shift as suggestive only until other changes landing in the same window are inspected. — reject
- `interest-is-not-cause`: Treat a metric, a logged event or a chart as showing interest only, pairing it with a commit or pull request citation before claiming cause. — reject
- `template-filler-discount`: Discount generic text in a mandatory rationale or template section and look for specific content. — reject
- `plan-date-staleness`: Compare a ticket's or spec's date with what shipped, since plans predate the implementation and go stale. — reject
- `casual-remark-not-a-decision`: Do not count a flippant remark before a commit as a decision, and look for considered discussion. — reject
- `generated-analysis-is-inference`: Use a tool's generated root-cause analysis as inference only, with the actual events and traces as the primary evidence. — reject
- `in-source-leads-only`: Follow references inside your own source and hand cross-source references on as leads without chasing them. — reject
- `counterfactual-strength-test`: Before rating a finding strong, ask whether it would still appear under a false interpretation and what would look different. — reject
- `ambiguity-left-open`: Report ambiguous evidence as ambiguous and leave an unresolved question unresolved over a confident fill-in. — reject
- `neighbor-evidence-substitution`: Do not offer evidence about a neighbouring feature as though it answers the question asked. — reject
- `evidence-record-template`: Have each investigator report its source, then direct items with location, author, date and relevance, and indirect items with inference chain and alternative readings. — reject
- `history-answer-frame`: Open a history answer by restating the question and orienting a cold reader to the code, and close it with confidence rated by sub-claim. — reject
- `competing-hypotheses-section`: When the record fits several stories, give each its evidence for and against, with no forced winner. — adopt → why#competing-hypotheses-section
- `one-reference-per-shared-source`: Give an item cited more than once a single authoritative reference. — reject
- `warehouse-evidence-inventory`: Look for warehouse evidence in product events, usage and billing events, experiment data, system tables and pipeline lineage. — defer
- `typed-models-over-raw`: Query a warehouse's deduplicated typed models, dropping to raw events only where no model serves. — defer
- `dbt-column-conventions`: Use the dbt model fields directly, the standard `_timestamp`, `_id`, `_auth_id`, `_request_id` and `event_name`, typed `properties_<name>` event properties and pre-extracted `context_` client fields, to save a describe round-trip. — reject
- `poll-running-query`: Poll a long-running query's handle for its result in place of running it again. — reject
- `probe-schema-before-query`: Confirm table and column names with listing and describe statements before querying a warehouse, and never report from an unverified table. — defer
- `schema-drift-check`: Check that a field existed when the target was written, since older data may lack it or hold it only in raw form. — defer
- `refresh-lag-fallback`: For events newer than a model's last refresh, query the raw table and deduplicate by id. — defer
- `timeline-against-ship-date`: Compare when a runtime or usage signal rose, fell, first appeared or stopped, and the releases it touched, with the date the target shipped. — defer
- `constant-origin-signal`: Treat a recorded distribution or monitor threshold that matches a constant in the code as evidence of where the number came from. — defer
- `warehouse-motive-signals`: Read an experiment's exposure counts and decision rows, and the expensive queries behind a migration, as warehouse evidence of motive. — defer
- `warehouse-finding-record`: Record each warehouse finding with its type, table, exact query, window, a compact numeric summary with no raw rows, its ship-date correlation and its strength. — defer
- `telemetry-evidence-inventory`: Look for telemetry evidence in metrics, monitors, dashboards, traces, logs, incidents and notebooks, where a metric's or monitor's existence itself shows concern. — defer
- `owning-service-first`: Find the services that own the target, and their dependencies, before searching telemetry. — defer
- `curated-views-before-raw`: Read the dashboards and monitors covering the target, noting their queries and thresholds, before raw telemetry. — defer
- `span-and-trace-inspection`: Use span statistics and specific traces for questions about timeouts, retries, slow paths and cross-service behaviour. — defer
- `narrow-log-lookups`: Narrow log searches by service, tag, text and a window around the change, aggregating in place of dumping raw logs. — defer
- `telemetry-motive-signals`: Read a dashboard by the target's author, an incident naming the code and a pre-change log pattern the guard would prevent as telemetry evidence of motive. — defer
- `telemetry-finding-record`: Record each telemetry item with its type, name, identifier, owner, dates, the condition or query that bears on the question and the strength of the connection. — defer
- `ticket-search-procedure`: Search an external ticket tracker's issues, comments, status updates, project documents, labels and milestones for business motive. — defer
- `named-record-first`: Fetch the records a seed commit names, with their comments, before searching by keyword. — adopt → why#named-record-first
- `target-derived-search-terms`: Build search terms from the target's feature name or business term, symbols, author, error strings and path, trying several wordings. — adopt → why#target-derived-search-terms
- `ship-window-bound`: Bound a search of a large source to a window around the date the target shipped. — reject
- `record-lineage-walk`: From a record, follow its parent and duplicate links to the item that carries the motive. — adopt → why#record-lineage-walk
- `ticket-motive-signals`: Read a stated business problem, a decision comment, an initiative-named parent, an attached spec and motive-bearing labels as tracker evidence of motive. — reject
- `record-finding-fields`: Record each evidence record with its identity, the exact motive quote and its location, its author, its dates and its linked records. — reject
- `ticket-external-metadata`: Record a ticket's labels, project and link with its finding. — reject
- `document-store-search-procedure`: Search a document store's requirement docs, specs, decision records, meeting notes, postmortems and runbooks with broad keywords for unlinked pages, following backlinks, child pages, meeting-note databases and authors' personal spaces. — defer
- `final-draft-preference`: Among several documents on a topic, use the finalized or most recently updated one. — reject
- `document-motive-signals`: Read a matching problem section, rejected approaches, a postmortem naming the fix, dated decision notes and a filled decision record as evidence of motive. — reject
- `document-external-metadata`: Record a document's URL and its final or draft status with its finding. — reject
- `error-trace-relevance`: Open a full error event to see whether its trace crosses the target and its tags and breadcrumbs match the guarded condition. — defer
- `orient-org-and-project`: When an error tracker's organization and project are unknown, look them up before searching. — reject
- `error-finding-record`: Record each error issue with its id, title, project, seen timestamps, event count with sampling, releases, a verbatim trace excerpt, ship-date correlation, link and author notes. — defer
- `chat-search-procedure`: Search team chat for deliberation by the author's messages around the merge date and by the pull request's link. — defer
- `inspect-chat-tool-schema-first`: Check which chat tool exists, its schema and whether it needs authentication before searching it. — reject

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/architect
- `stub-body-sketch`: Express the shape as signatures and types with stub bodies, pseudocode for tricky logic and comments stating intent and invariants, so that types and signatures alone reveal the data flow, as one file for a small change and a module map for larger work. — adopt → codebase-design#stub-body-sketch
- `phase-todos`: Open a task list with one item per phase before beginning. — reject
- `grounded-sketch`: Before sketching, build a working model of what the design touches and write its architectural explanation, since naming a file is not grounding, skipping this only for true greenfield work. — adopt → codebase-design#grounded-sketch
- `ownership-change-rationale`: When a design changes who owns what or how layers divide, also investigate why the existing shape exists so that its reason becomes a constraint. — adopt → codebase-design#ownership-change-rationale
- `sketch-by-parallel-runners`: Produce candidates through parallel runners on different models, each in its own workspace and told not to hedge, then pick a base on named design axes. — defer
- `role-model-config-line`: Read each spawned role's model from a named line of a shared configuration, falling back to a fixed default and leaving the field unset for an alias. — reject
- `sketch-required-twice`: Require two or more structurally different whole-shape candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks adequate. — reject
- `design-red-flag-screen`: Screen every candidate shape against a named list of design flaws before choosing it, treating any hit as grounds to revise or reject the shape. — adopt → codebase-design#design-red-flag-screen
- `next-agent-test`: Prefer a design where an edit that looks right from one file is right everywhere, assuming the next editor sees only the files it opened and copies the nearest example. — adopt → codebase-design#next-agent-test
- `depth-as-leverage`: Prefer modules whose manageable interface hides a large amount of useful behaviour. — adopt → codebase-design#depth-as-leverage
- `shallow-module-signs`: Treat callers coordinating several methods for one operation, options exposing internal stages, and an interface that does not spare learning the implementation as signs of a shallow module. — adopt → codebase-design#shallow-module-signs
- `leaked-decision-flag`: Reject a design in which one internal decision appears in several modules, so that changing it needs coordinated edits. — adopt → codebase-design#leaked-decision-flag
- `knowledge-not-phase-modules`: Organise modules around one body of domain knowledge, not around execution phases such as load, validate, transform and save. — reject
- `pass-through-flag`: Remove a method that forwards the same arguments with the same shape, unless it adds policy, adaptation or a distinct abstraction. — adopt → codebase-design#pass-through-flag
- `split-ownership-flag`: Give each piece of state one owner, so that others read it or ask the owner to change it, with no second writer and no copy. — adopt → codebase-design#split-ownership-flag
- `one-way-per-task`: Keep a single way to do a task, moving callers off the others and deleting them in the same change. — adopt → codebase-design#one-way-per-task
- `unreachable-internals`: Make a module's internals unreachable, so that an import from outside fails the build. — adopt → codebase-design#unreachable-internals
- `derived-or-checked-lists`: Derive duplicate lists from one, or make the build fail when lists that cannot be derived disagree. — adopt → codebase-design#derived-or-checked-lists
- `synthesis-decision-record`: Record the chosen base candidate with its reason, what was grafted from the rest and why each was rejected. — reject
- `sketch-opt-in-checkpoint`: Proceed from the sketch without a human stop unless the invoker asks for one. — reject
- `sketch-commit-first`: Commit the agreed sketch separately before implementing it. — reject
- `fill-in-breakage`: Accept scoped, planned breakage while filling in a sketch. — reject
- `pushback-triggers-regrounding`: Treat a human objection to the shape as grounding evidence that forces a return to grounding and sketching before more code. — reject
- `implement-against-sketch`: Build against the sketch as the contract, surfacing any departure and revising the sketch first when the code must diverge. — adopt → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/feature.md
- `scrap-on-repeated-friction`: Discard a sketch when implementation repeatedly shows a pattern that it is wrong, such as recurring workarounds, special-case branches, type escape hatches or repeated deviations, and not on isolated problems. — reject
- `scrap-redesign-procedure`: After scrapping, re-explain what exists, redesign as if the new constraints were known from the start, shrink below the old sketch before growing and rerun the candidates. — reject
- `sketch-rationale`: Ship a one-page rationale with the sketch covering the problem and its constraints, the shape with invariants, validation, non-goals and depth, the tradeoffs accepted, at least one rejected alternative, and open questions phrased as questions. — adopt → codebase-design#sketch-rationale
- `caller-usage-first`: Write callers' usage first and derive the types from it, reconciling any divergence toward the usage. — adopt → codebase-design#caller-usage-first
- `next-step-sentence`: State in one sentence what gets built first from the sketch. — reject
- `dominant-access-shape`: Settle the core types first and trace each dominant access pattern through them before writing the logic. — reject
- `no-later-index-gate`: Treat a structure that answers an access pattern with a map, index or cache to be added later as wrong. — reject
- `concurrent-modification-test`: Before sharing state between actors, ask what a concurrent modification would do, and isolate the state unless the answer is nothing. — reject
- `eliminate-shared-writes`: Before coordinating concurrent writers, give each its own write target (file, key, branch or directory) and merge only where results are read. — reject
- `invariant-enforcement-ranking`: Prefer hard-to-misuse types to runtime checks, and runtime checks to comments, for enforcing an invariant. — reject
- `boundary-validation`: Concentrate validation, narrowing and error handling where data crosses a system boundary such as CLI arguments, configuration, the network or an external API. — reject
- `trust-internal-types`: Inside the system, trust data that a boundary already validated into types and propagate errors instead of re-checking it in every layer. — reject
- `pure-core-thin-shell`: Keep business logic in pure functions free of framework dependencies, leaving a thin mechanical shell that calls them. — reject
- `domain-not-wire-types`: Expose domain concepts across a public surface, never the transport, storage or framework types behind it. — reject
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit. — reject
- `repeat-and-crash-question`: Ask what happens when a state change runs twice or crashes halfway, and make the transition idempotent where applicable. — reject
- `call-chain-file-limit`: Flatten the hierarchy when following the flow takes more than three files. — reject

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-boundary-discipline
- `boundary-validation`: Concentrate validation, narrowing and error handling where data crosses a system boundary such as CLI arguments, configuration, the network or an external API. — adopt → principle-boundary-discipline#boundary-validation
- `trust-internal-types`: Inside the system, trust data that a boundary already validated into types and propagate errors instead of re-checking it in every layer. — adopt → principle-boundary-discipline#scoped-internal-trust
- `domain-not-wire-types`: Expose domain concepts across a public surface, never the transport, storage or framework types behind it. — adopt → principle-boundary-discipline#domain-not-wire-types
- `policy-at-edge`: Keep general-purpose mechanism inside a module and special-purpose policy at its edge. — defer
- `parse-at-boundary`: Turn raw external input into typed domain values with a parse function at the boundary where it enters. — adopt → principle-boundary-discipline#parse-at-boundary
- `pure-core-thin-shell`: Keep business logic in pure functions free of framework dependencies, leaving a thin mechanical shell that calls them. — adopt → principle-boundary-discipline#pure-core-thin-shell

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-exhaust-the-design-space
- `competing-prototypes`: Before committing to an interaction or architecture with no precedent in the codebase, or to a product decision whose experience depends on feel, build two or three competing prototypes and compare them side by side. — adopt → prototype#competing-prototypes

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-foundational-thinking
- `data-shape-first`: Settle the core types and data structures, traced against every access pattern, before writing the logic that uses them. — adopt → principle-model-the-domain#data-shape-first
- `structural-dry`: Deduplicate structure such as types and data models, but tolerate a few similar statements rather than a premature abstraction. — adopt → principle-model-the-domain#structural-dry
- `behaviour-and-edge-case-tests`: Judge tests by the behaviours and edge cases they exercise, not by line coverage. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#behaviour-and-edge-case-tests
- `concurrent-modification-test`: Before sharing state between actors, ask what a concurrent modification would do, and isolate the state unless the answer is nothing. — adopt → principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state#concurrent-modification-test
- `scaffold-first`: Sequence first the work every later phase benefits from (CI, linting, test infrastructure, shared types) before features. — defer
- `test-before-fix`: Sequence the test that will check a fix before the fix itself. — reject
- `small-single-purpose-commits`: Keep each commit small and about one thing. — adopt → principle-sequence-verifiable-units#small-single-purpose-commits
- `coherent-increment`: Make each increment land or deepen one coherent abstraction instead of spreading a new capability across callers as special-case coordination. — adopt → principle-model-the-domain#coherent-increment
- `subtraction-first`: Before adding to a system, remove the complexity in its way (such as dead code, redundant validators and stub references), then build on the simpler base. — adopt → principle-subtract-before-you-add#touched-scope-subtraction

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-make-operations-idempotent
- `convergent-operations`: Design state-changing operations to converge on the same correct end state however often they run and wherever a previous run stopped. — adopt → principle-make-operations-idempotent#convergent-operations
- `reconcile-from-state`: Derive each step from the observed current state compared with the goal, applying only the difference. — adopt → principle-make-operations-idempotent#reconcile-from-state
- `judgeable-leftovers`: Make everything a run leaves behind (locks, temporary files, partial records, claims) recognisable as stale by the next run, using evidence that holds wherever the run stopped. — adopt → principle-make-operations-idempotent#judgeable-leftovers
- `interruption-point-audit`: Check a state-changing operation by asking what happens when it runs twice and when it stops at each point, and add reconciliation wherever the answer depends on leftovers. — adopt → principle-make-operations-idempotent#interruption-point-audit

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-minimize-reader-load
- `reader-load-axes`: Judge maintainability by the layers a reader must trace and the state they must hold, not by line counts, complexity scores or architecture labels. — adopt → principle-minimize-reader-load#reader-load-axes
- `collapse-thin-layers`: Inline layers that cost more than they save, such as one-caller wrappers, adapters with no second implementation and speculative indirection. — adopt → principle-minimize-reader-load#collapse-thin-layers
- `deletion-test`: Question a layer that only forwards and keep one whose removal would spread complexity across callers. — adopt → codebase-design#deletion-test
- `depth-as-leverage`: Prefer modules whose manageable interface hides a large amount of useful behaviour. — adopt → codebase-design#depth-as-leverage
- `return-not-mutate`: Design functions to return results rather than cause side effects, so behaviour can be observed directly. — adopt → codebase-design#return-not-mutate
- `narrowest-state-scope`: Give state the narrowest scope that works: locals over fields over module state over globals. — adopt → principle-minimize-reader-load#narrowest-state-scope
- `derive-over-sync`: Derive a value from its source when needed instead of storing a copy that must be kept in sync. — adopt → principle-minimize-reader-load#derive-over-sync
- `invariant-at-boundary`: Name an invariant once, at the boundary that owns it, rather than in every consumer. — adopt → principle-minimize-reader-load#invariant-at-boundary
- `reader-load-net-test`: Before adding a layer or a piece of state, check that it removes at least as much reader load elsewhere as it adds. — adopt → principle-minimize-reader-load#reader-load-net-test
- `thirty-second-trace-test`: Check that a new reader can say where a value comes from and what can change it in under thirty seconds. — reject

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-model-the-domain
- `structure-over-conditionals`: Encode domain rules in a fitting data structure (state machine, typed model, lookup table, union, reducer) instead of conditionals scattered across the code. — adopt → principle-model-the-domain#structure-over-conditionals
- `knowledge-not-phase-modules`: Organise modules around one body of domain knowledge, not around execution phases such as load, validate, transform and save. — adopt → principle-model-the-domain#knowledge-not-phase-modules
- `no-forced-abstraction`: Keep boring code that is clear, local and unlikely to grow, adding indirection only when it removes branches, duplicated rules, invalid states or lifecycle risk. — adopt → principle-model-the-domain#no-forced-abstraction

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-redesign-from-first-principles
- `foundational-requirement-redesign`: Integrate a new requirement by designing as if it had been a founding assumption, after reading the affected design, rather than bolting it on. — adopt → principle-redesign-from-first-principles#proposed-foundational-redesign
- `full-propagation`: Carry a design change through every reference to it (types, documents, examples, rationale) so no stale trace remains. — adopt → principle-redesign-from-first-principles#full-propagation
- `whole-design-incremental-delivery`: Think a redesign through as a whole before starting, then deliver it in increments rather than in one drop. — adopt → principle-redesign-from-first-principles#whole-design-incremental-delivery

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
- `eliminate-shared-writes`: Before coordinating concurrent writers, give each its own write target (file, key, branch or directory) and merge only where results are read. — adopt → principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state#eliminate-shared-writes
- `structural-serialization`: When one shared write target is a real invariant, serialize access by structure (lock, sequential phase, single writer, compare-and-swap), never by instruction. — adopt → principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state#structural-serialization

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — skill:pstack/skills/principle-type-system-discipline
- `unrepresentable-invalid-states`: Shape types so the checker rejects impossible states, defining special cases out of existence instead of handling them. — adopt → principle-type-system-discipline#unrepresentable-invalid-states
- `exhaustive-variant-handling`: Handle every variant of a closed type so the checker reports a variant left unhandled. — adopt → principle-type-system-discipline#exhaustive-variant-handling
- `branded-primitives`: Give semantically distinct values that share a primitive type their own types, validated once at creation and trusted afterwards. — adopt → principle-type-system-discipline#branded-primitives
- `parse-at-boundary`: Turn raw external input into typed domain values with a parse function at the boundary where it enters. — adopt → principle-boundary-discipline#parse-at-boundary
- `schema-derived-types`: Derive types from the authoritative schema that owns a shape instead of hand-writing a parallel type. — adopt → principle-type-system-discipline#schema-derived-types

#### engineering · Design · Decomposition — skill:pstack/skills/principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
- `same-wave-legacy-removal`: When an internal API with no external dependants is replaced as part of a simplification, in a project that can absorb a coordinated breaking change, migrate every caller and delete the old API in the same change instead of keeping a compatibility layer. — adopt → principle-migrate-without-shims#same-wave-legacy-removal
- `implementation-test-deletion`: When internals change, rewrite or delete tests that only protect the old implementation, asserting the current contract instead. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#implementation-test-deletion

#### engineering · Design · Decomposition — skill:pstack/skills/principle-outcome-oriented-execution
- `declared-breakage-window`: In a planned migration, accept declared, scoped and reversible intermediate breakage instead of writing throwaway compatibility code to keep every step green. — adopt → principle-migrate-without-shims#migration-group-unit
- `touched-area-checks`: During a migration, keep fast high-signal checks running on the areas being changed. — adopt → principle-migrate-without-shims#touched-area-checks
- `full-verification-at-completion`: At the end of a planned migration or rewrite, run full static and runtime verification, not only the checks the last change touched. — adopt → principle-migrate-without-shims#full-verification-at-completion

#### engineering · Design · Decomposition — skill:pstack/skills/principle-subtract-before-you-add
- `subtraction-first`: Before adding to a system, remove the complexity in its way (such as dead code, redundant validators and stub references), then build on the simpler base. — adopt → principle-subtract-before-you-add#touched-scope-subtraction
- `leave-it-simpler`: Leave each touched design slightly simpler and more capable, behind the same or a smaller surface, than it was found. — reject
- `cut-before-polish`: Reach the minimum version before investing in its quality. — adopt → principle-subtract-before-you-add#cut-before-polish
- `present-requirement-only`: Add an abstraction, dependency or feature only for a present requirement, never a speculative one. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `decision-relevance-pruning`: Keep only content that changes the agent's decisions, such as conventions, non-obvious failure modes, required interfaces and invariants. — reject
- `stub-deletion`: Delete a reference that carries no novel content instead of leaving a stub that points elsewhere. — adopt → principle-subtract-before-you-add#stub-deletion

#### engineering · Design · Specification — skill:pstack/skills/principle-experience-first
- `experience-over-convenience`: When implementation convenience conflicts with the consumer's experience, choose the experience. — adopt → principle-experience-first#experience-over-convenience
- `justified-surface`: Every feature, control and option must earn its place against the core workflow; cut what does not serve it. — adopt → principle-experience-first#justified-surface
- `polish-over-breadth`: Ship fewer finished features rather than more rough ones. — adopt → principle-experience-first#polish-over-breadth
- `throwaway-design-first`: Settle a design decision in a throwaway artifact before writing production code for it. — reject
- `detail-finish`: Finish interaction details such as transitions, alignment, spacing, feedback and error states as part of the work, not as later polish. — adopt → principle-experience-first#detail-finish
- `consumer-as-user`: Treat whoever consumes the work (end user, importing colleague, next maintainer) as its user, and explain impact from their side. — adopt → principle-experience-first#consumer-as-user

#### engineering · Building · Diagnosis — skill:pstack/skills/benchmark-checklist
- `run-evidence-answers`: Settle every vetting question with data from an actual run, never from reasoning about the code. — adopt → performance-optimization#run-evidence-answers
- `confound-elimination`: List what else a number could be measuring (errors, skipped or cached work, code that never ran, an untuned side, noise, a negligible share) and rule each out with evidence. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#confound-elimination
- `ballpark-path`: For a rough figure the user asked for, let one run do while still checking errors and that the work happened, saying it is one run, and applying the other checks only if the run looks wrong. — adopt → performance-optimization#ballpark-path
- `choice-never-ballpark`: Never let a measurement that chooses between options take the rough one-run path. — adopt → performance-optimization#choice-never-ballpark
- `shipped-claim-first`: Before any run, write the exact result sentence you expect to publish, with its metric and dataset, and test the vetting questions against that sentence. — adopt → performance-optimization#shipped-claim-first
- `script-reading-first`: Read the measuring script before a run and note what it times, what it counts and what it leaves out. — adopt → performance-optimization#script-reading-first
- `machine-load-check`: Before measuring, check the load average and core count and find what is occupying a busy machine. — adopt → performance-optimization#machine-load-check
- `interleave-unstoppable-load`: When competing load cannot be stopped, run the compared sides in turn so the noise hits both equally, and disclose that in the report. — adopt → performance-optimization#interleave-unstoppable-load
- `named-limiter`: Explain a measured number by the resource or code path that bounds it, found from a profile or counters taken during the run and mapped to source, not from reading code. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#named-limiter
- `unreported-profile-run`: Profile and trace in a separate run whose numbers are never reported, because instrumentation distorts timing. — adopt → performance-optimization#unreported-profile-run
- `per-process-cpu-read`: Inspect CPU use per process when hunting a limiter. — adopt → performance-optimization#per-process-cpu-read
- `runtime-profiler-read`: Use a language or system profiler when hunting a limiter. — adopt → performance-optimization#runtime-profiler-read
- `io-wait-read`: Inspect I/O wait when hunting a limiter. — adopt → performance-optimization#io-wait-read
- `syscall-count-read`: Inspect system call counts when hunting a limiter. — adopt → performance-optimization#kernel-time-syscall-count
- `load-generator-saturation`: Watch the load generator during a run, since a saturated generator means the result describes it and not the target. — adopt → performance-optimization#load-generator-saturation
- `limiter-before-dismissal`: When a change leaves the number unmoved, find the limiter before concluding the change has no value. — adopt → performance-optimization#limiter-before-dismissal
- `production-parity-sides`: Run every compared side as production runs it: release builds, flags and environment, batching and transactions, connection pools, cache temperature, and the same versions and data. — adopt → performance-optimization#production-parity-sides
- `defaults-compare-configurations`: Treat a result with one side on defaults as a comparison of configurations and not of implementations. — adopt → performance-optimization#config-mismatch-comparison
- `settings-limiter-untuned`: Treat a side whose limiter is a setting, such as per-row commits, a debug build or a missing index, as untuned. — adopt → performance-optimization#settings-limiter-untuned
- `tuned-before-winner`: Tune an untuned side and measure again before naming a winner, and name none from a run whose side cannot be tuned. — adopt → performance-optimization#tuned-claim-gate
- `no-narrowing-for-adoption`: When someone is choosing what to adopt, do not cure an untuned comparison by narrowing the claim to today's as-shipped settings. — adopt → performance-optimization#no-narrowing-for-adoption
- `capacity-arithmetic`: Check throughput in bytes against disk and network capacity and operations per second times cost per operation against available cores, and read a result past a limit as having measured something else, for example a cache, a no-op or a defect. — adopt → performance-optimization#capacity-arithmetic
- `share-bound-on-gain`: Bound a claimed gain by the fraction f of elapsed time the changed part takes: for 0 <= f < 1, elapsed-time reduction is at most f and the matching throughput speedup at most 1/(1-f), at f = 1 the model gives no finite speedup bound, and a reported percentage names which it is. — adopt → performance-optimization#share-bound-on-gain
- `failure-count`: Count failures and non-success responses, adding the count when the measuring script has none, because fast rejections and slow timeouts both skew timing. — adopt → performance-optimization#failure-count
- `correct-output-check`: Check that a measured run's outputs are correct and not merely present. — adopt → performance-optimization#correct-output-check
- `five-run-floor`: Run each compared side at least five times. — adopt → performance-optimization#comparison-run-floor
- `alternated-sides`: Alternate the compared sides run by run so warmup, lazy initialization, caches and drift favour neither. — adopt → performance-optimization#alternated-sides
- `median-and-range-report`: Report the median and the range across a comparison's runs. — adopt → performance-optimization#median-and-range-report
- `within-variation-no-difference`: Give a gap smaller than run-to-run variation the verdict no measurable difference. — adopt → performance-optimization#resolved-no-difference
- `close-call-statistics`: When a comparison is close, test the gap with a rank-sum test or statistics the harness provides. — adopt → performance-optimization#close-call-statistics
- `end-to-end-share`: Beside any micro result, measure the whole path a user waits on under realistic sizes and concurrency, and state the micro result as its share. — adopt → performance-optimization#end-to-end-share
- `work-ran-check`: Prove the work happened inside the timed span and the code used its result, since lazy code, discarded results and timeouts can produce numbers for work that never happened. — adopt → performance-optimization#work-ran-check
- `one-verdict-first`: Open a measurement report with one verdict: slower, faster, inconclusive or no measurable difference. — adopt → performance-optimization#one-verdict-first
- `evidence-with-number`: Report a measured number together with its run count, spread and limiter. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#evidence-with-number
- `measurement-unit`: State every reported number with its unit. — adopt → performance-optimization#measurement-unit
- `no-limiter-inconclusive`: Call a claimed difference inconclusive when its limiter cannot be named. — adopt → performance-optimization#no-limiter-inconclusive
- `untuned-side-inconclusive`: Call a verdict inconclusive when a side ran untuned. — adopt → performance-optimization#tuned-claim-gate
- `unchecked-run-inconclusive`: Call a verdict inconclusive when the error or work check could not be done. — adopt → performance-optimization#unchecked-run-inconclusive
- `inconclusive-names-gap`: Have an inconclusive verdict state which check or condition caused it. — adopt → performance-optimization#inconclusive-names-gap
- `one-number-pr-body`: Keep a pull request body to one primary number, with the supporting evidence linked from it. — defer
- `vet-at-flow-gates`: In a performance flow, vet the baseline before planning from it, every later number, and a harness before it is frozen. — reject
- `harness-prints-counts`: Make a frozen harness emit error and work counts, which hands each keep-or-revert decision those two checks. — adopt → performance-optimization#harness-prints-counts

#### engineering · Building · Diagnosis — skill:pstack/skills/principle-attack-the-premise
- `premise-test-gate`: After two or more fixes that rest on one premise fail the same gate, write that premise as one sentence and test it with an observation that would differ were it false, before any further fix that assumes it. — adopt → principle-attack-the-premise#premise-test-gate
- `owning-layer-fix`: Fix a bug at the layer that owns it rather than patching around it. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md

#### engineering · Building · Diagnosis — skill:pstack/skills/principle-explain-the-number
- `decision-before-measurement`: Before measuring, name the result that would change a decision and the noise floor the result must clear. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#decision-before-measurement
- `noise-inconclusive`: Treat a measured difference within noise as inconclusive rather than as a gain or a loss. — adopt → performance-optimization#noise-inconclusive
- `named-limiter`: Explain a measured number by the resource or code path that bounds it, found from a profile or counters taken during the run and mapped to source, not from reading code. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#named-limiter
- `confound-elimination`: List what else a number could be measuring (errors, skipped or cached work, code that never ran, an untuned side, noise, a negligible share) and rule each out with evidence. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#confound-elimination
- `evidence-with-number`: Report a measured number together with its run count, spread and limiter. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#evidence-with-number
- `eval-result-scrutiny`: Before trusting an eval result, check that every run did the task, that the gap holds across trials and models, and that the scenario matters. — adopt → principle-explain-the-number#eval-result-scrutiny

#### engineering · Building · Diagnosis — skill:pstack/skills/principle-fix-root-causes
- `owning-layer-fix`: Fix a bug at the layer that owns it rather than patching around it. — adopt → doc:AGENTS.md
- `reproduction-first`: Obtain a reproduction that shows the reported failure, not a nearby one, before diagnosing it. — reject
- `why-chain`: Ask why at each step of a failure until the answer is a wrong decision in the code rather than a consequence of an earlier one. — adopt → principle-fix-root-causes#why-chain
- `observe-not-guess`: When stuck, add instrumentation and read the actual error and state instead of reasoning from guesses. — reject
- `legitimate-state-test`: Before guarding where a symptom surfaced, decide whether the triggering state is legitimate: handle a legitimate state there, and trace an illegitimate one to what produced it. — adopt → principle-fix-root-causes#legitimate-state-test
- `persisted-state-suspect`: When a failure appears only after a restart, suspect persisted state (configuration, caches, lock files, serialized state) first. — adopt → principle-fix-root-causes#persisted-state-suspect
- `fix-every-instance`: Search for every place with the same fault and fix them all, not only the reported instance. — adopt → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md
- `workaround-comment-smell`: Treat a workaround that needs a long justifying comment as a sign the code is wrong, and fix the code instead. — defer
- `always-on-signal`: After a fact took a deep investigation to find, propose the cheap always-on signal that would have shown it at first look. — adopt → doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md

#### engineering · Building · Implementation — skill:pstack/skills/principle-laziness-protocol
- `deletion-bias`: When refactoring or tempted to add an abstraction, layer or threaded signal, prefer deleting code to adding it. — adopt → principle-subtract-before-you-add#deletion-bias
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit. — adopt → principle-subtract-before-you-add#single-source-of-truth

#### engineering · Building · Implementation — skill:pstack/skills/principle-sequence-verifiable-units
- `verified-unit-sequence`: Split multi-step work into small units that each end in a checked state, and start the next only when the current one passes. — adopt → principle-sequence-verifiable-units#verified-unit-sequence
- `clean-baseline-first`: Start from a clean, current base so each check measures against the real baseline. — adopt → principle-sequence-verifiable-units#baseline-check-before-change
- `argument-order-commits`: Order commits so the history proves the work (failing test before fix, removal before reshape, baseline before treatment, scaffold before feature), each commit standing alone. — adopt → principle-sequence-verifiable-units#argument-order-commits

- `satisfies-over-cast`: Check a value against a type with an operator that keeps its literal types, in place of a cast. — defer
- `parse-at-boundary`: Turn raw external input into typed domain values with a parse function at the boundary where it enters. — reject
- `loose-record-stops-at-parse`: Allow a string-keyed unknown record, under any alias, to exist only up to the parse. — defer
- `trust-internal-types`: Inside the system, trust data that a boundary already validated into types and propagate errors instead of re-checking it in every layer. — reject
- `wire-parse-ignores-unknown-fields`: Parse wire formats with unknown fields ignored so forward-compatible changes do not break old clients. — defer
- `persisted-json-versioned`: Store persisted JSON as a versioned blob. — defer
- `persisted-json-guarded-parse`: Surround the parse of persisted JSON with an error handler. — defer
- `schema-derived-types`: Derive types from the authoritative schema that owns a shape instead of hand-writing a parallel type. — adopt → principle-type-system-discipline#schema-derived-types
- `type-utilities-before-new-interface`: Try the language's type utilities before declaring a new interface. — defer
- `object-arguments`: Pass a single object in place of positional arguments so order is irrelevant and calls read clearly. — defer
- `hot-path-positional-exception`: Skip object arguments on per-frame rendering, tokenizers, parsers and other tight loops where allocation matters. — defer
- `no-mocking-what-can-run`: Mock only what cannot run locally, and avoid mocks for anything that can. — reject
- `real-test-primitives-with-leak-checks`: Prefer the framework's real test primitives along with leak and disposable checks. — defer
- `verify-ui-in-running-build`: Confirm interface behaviour in an actual running build. — defer
- `diagnostics-traceable-from-id`: Emit diagnostics through a structured logger carrying enough detail to trace a problem starting from an id. — defer
- `no-console-log-in-shipped-code`: Forbid console logging in code that ships. — defer

#### engineering · Verification · Testing — skill:pstack/skills/principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
- `meaningful-behaviour-assertion`: Assert meaningful results, state or boundary interactions at a stable boundary rather than internal call choreography. — adopt → tdd#meaningful-behaviour-assertion
- `two-edit-test-judgement`: Judge every test by two imagined edits: breaking the behaviour must fail it, and restructuring the internals must not. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#two-edit-test-judgement
- `independent-expectation`: Derive expected values from an independent source such as a spec, worked example or trusted fixture, never computing both sides with the implementation under test. — adopt → tdd#independent-expectation
- `hollow-test-forms`: Check a test for the usual hollow forms: an assertion looser than the contract, a restated constant the code never reads, or an assertion on data the test built itself. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#hollow-test-forms
- `implementation-test-deletion`: When internals change, rewrite or delete tests that only protect the old implementation, asserting the current contract instead. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#implementation-test-deletion
- `public-interface-testing`: Exercise behaviour in tests through public interfaces. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#public-interface-testing
- `contract-exact-assertion`: Assert exactly what the contract promises, no less and no more, letting the contract decide whether a call, an absence, a payload or an error type is behaviour. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#contract-exact-assertion
- `absence-positive-control`: Pair an assertion that something did not happen with a positive case showing the same test would see it happen. — adopt → principle-test-behavior-not-implementation#absence-positive-control

#### engineering · Verification · Testing — skill:pstack/skills/tdd
- `red-green`: Make one test fail before implementing the change that makes it pass. — adopt → tdd#red-green
- `test-skipped-when-impractical`: Add no new test when it would demand wide harness setup, fragile mocks, slow full-stack infrastructure, production-only state, unclear reproduction or heavy unrelated fixtures, and never build a test path from nothing just to follow the workflow. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#optional-regression-test-skip
- `bug-understanding-checklist`: Identify intended behaviour, current behaviour, the affected path and the smallest observable reproduction. — reject
- `closest-existing-test-kind`: Prefer the kind of test already used for that codepath. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#closest-existing-test-kind
- `no-implementation-coupling`: Avoid tests coupled to the implementation's internal structure, so they survive behaviour-preserving refactors. — adopt → tdd#no-implementation-coupling
- `failure-for-the-right-reason`: Run a new test before fixing and, if it passes or fails for another reason, correct the test or reproduction first. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#failure-for-the-right-reason
- `contract-preserving-fix`: Make the smallest production change that gives the intended behaviour and preserves neighbouring contracts. — reject
- `closest-executable-fallback`: When a failing test is impractical, substitute a targeted script, reproduction command, browser automation, snapshot diff, log assertion or narrow integration check. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#closest-executable-fallback
- `no-test-over-bad-test`: Prefer adding nothing to a test that mostly exercises mocks, encodes internals, depends on timing or global state, needs costly infrastructure for a minor fix, or would be discarded right after. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#no-test-over-bad-test
- `no-tests-bent-or-weakened`: Do not change tests to agree with wrong behaviour, and keep existing assertions as strong unless expected behaviour truly changed for a clear reason. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#no-tests-bent-or-weakened
- `focused-regression-test`: Write the smallest test focused on this bug, without broad fixture changes or added unrelated coverage. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#focused-regression-test
- `flaky-test-names-its-signal`: For a flaky bug, remove nondeterminism from the test as far as possible and document which signal it pins. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#flaky-test-names-its-signal
- `focused-first-then-siblings`: When a bug reveals a wider failure class, land the focused regression first and only then consider related coverage. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#focused-first-then-siblings
- `before-after-proof-report`: Name the check that failed before the fix with its failure, and the passing run after the fix with any nearby validation. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#before-after-proof-report
- `missing-red-explained`: If a failure before the fix could not be shown, say why and describe the substitute check. — adopt, pending cr-r2pa.2.18 → tdd#missing-red-explained

#### core · Discovery · Charting — skill:skills/engineering/wayfinder

- `destination-first`: Name the destination first, since it fixes the scope and shapes every ticket. — adopt → wayfinder#destination-first

- `local-tracker-default`: Default to a local markdown tracker when no tracker is configured. — defer

- `grilling-default-type`: Make a live interview the default ticket type. — defer
- `fog-hygiene`: Keep decided, ticketed and out-of-scope items out of the map's section of not-yet-specified questions. — adopt → wayfinder#fog-hygiene

- `low-res-map-load`: When working a map, load only its low-resolution body and open related tickets only on demand. — adopt → wayfinder#low-res-map-load

- `invalidated-ticket-reconciliation`: Update or delete the other tickets that a recorded decision invalidated. — adopt → wayfinder#invalidated-ticket-reconciliation

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:skills/productivity/writing-for-agents
- `context-pointers`: Write a pointer that names the material and the condition for reaching it, front-loading the trigger. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#context-pointers
- `two-loads`: Weigh always-loaded context cost on the agent against cognitive load on the human. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#two-loads
- `inline-vs-disclose`: Inline what every branch needs and disclose branch-specific material behind a conditional pointer. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#inline-vs-disclose
- `co-location`: Keep a concept's definition, rules and caveats under one heading so reading one part brings its neighbours. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#co-location
- `completion-criteria-clarity`: End each step on an observable, checkable done-or-not-done criterion that resists premature completion. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#completion-criteria-clarity
- `completion-criteria-demand`: Phrase the criterion to demand thorough work, driving the legwork latent in its wording. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#completion-criteria-demand
- `split-by-invocation`: Split off a model-invoked skill only when a distinct leading word should trigger it or another skill must reach it. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#split-by-invocation
- `sequence-isolation`: Split a run of steps so later post-completion steps stay out of view, driving more legwork on the step in front. — defer
- `leading-words`: Anchor behaviour in a compact pretrained concept repeated as a token, reaching for an existing word before coining one. — defer
- `negation-avoidance`: Steer by the positive target because negation makes the forbidden behaviour more available, keeping prohibitions a last-resort guardrail. — defer
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#single-source-of-truth
- `environment-as-cache`: Point to authoritative commands and lookups instead of copying volatile facts the agent can find itself. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#environment-as-cache
- `relevance-check`: Check every line still bears on the document's task, pruning stale or irrelevant ones. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#relevance-check
- `no-op-deletion`: Delete instructions the model already follows by default. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#no-op-deletion
- `invocation-mode`: Choose model-invoked or user-invoked activation, setting the disable-model-invocation flag for manual workflows. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#invocation-mode
- `shared-reference-home`: Put reference several skills need in one model-invoked, all-reference skill they can each invoke. — defer

- `sharpen-before-inline`: Fix a weakly reached must-have target by sharpening its pointer's wording first, inlining it only if that fails. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#sharpen-before-inline
- `one-trigger-per-branch`: Give each trigger branch of a pointer one trigger, collapsing synonyms. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#one-trigger-per-branch
- `pointer-identity-trim`: Cut from a pointer any identity the target's own body already carries. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#pointer-identity-trim
- `criterion-before-isolation`: Sharpen a vague completion criterion before considering hiding the later steps. — defer
- `triad-collapse`: Hunt restated triads and long gestures and collapse each into a single leading word. — defer
- `model-facing-description`: Write a model-invoked skill's description as a model-facing pointer listing its trigger branches. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#activation-boundary
- `human-facing-description`: Write a user-invoked skill's description as a one-line human summary with triggers stripped. — defer
- `external-shared-reference`: Put reference shared by user-invoked skills in a plain external file rather than a skill. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#surface-choice
- `observed-rushing-context-isolation`: Hide post-completion steps only after sharpening the completion criterion has failed and rushing is observed, and only across a real context boundary such as a handoff or subagent. — defer
- `empirical-instruction-default-check`: Settle whether an instruction changes behaviour from the model's default by running the document, not by debate. — adopt → authoring-for-agents#verification

#### core · U · Tutoring — skill:skills/productivity/teach

- `always-stateful-course`: Treat every teaching request as a stateful multi-session course kept in the workspace. — defer

- `spacing`: Space practice over time to build long-term retention. — adopt → teach#spacing

- `learning-records`: ADR-like records of lessons and established prior knowledge that steer what to teach next. — adopt → teach#learning-records
- `quiz-equal-length`: Make every quiz answer the same number of words, and characters where possible, so formatting gives nothing away. — defer
- `vary-answer-position`: Vary which position holds the correct answer across questions so order gives nothing away. — adopt → teach#vary-answer-position
- `wisdom-community-referral`: For questions needing real-world wisdom, attempt an answer but ultimately refer the learner to a high-reputation community. — defer
- `reference-sheets`: Build durable quick-reference documents that outlive the lessons that spawned them. — defer
- `preference-notes`: Record the learner's stated teaching preferences in a notes file to steer future lessons. — defer
- `sourced-explanations`: Draw explanations from trusted, cited sources and check unfamiliar or changing facts rather than relying on unverified recall. — adopt → teach#sourced-explanations
- `tight-feedback-loop`: Teach skills through an interactive feedback loop that is as tight and immediate, ideally automatic, as possible. — defer
- `knowledge-skills-wisdom-frame`: Frame learning as knowledge from trusted sources, skills from interactive lessons and wisdom from communities. — adopt → teach#knowledge-skills-wisdom-frame
- `resource-gathering-priority`: Prioritise finding high-quality resources until the resources file is well populated. — defer
- `polished-lesson-typography`: Make lessons visually polished with clean typography so they serve later review. — defer
- `open-artifact-for-user`: Open a generated artifact for the user with the platform's opener and give its path. — defer
- `cross-linked-lessons`: Cross-link lessons to other lessons and reference documents. — adopt → teach#cross-linked-lessons
- `lesson-primary-source`: Recommend one top primary source with each lesson. — defer
- `follow-up-prompt`: Remind the learner in each lesson to ask follow-up questions. — defer
- `mission-interview-first`: When the learning mission is unclear or empty, ask the learner why they want to learn before teaching. — adopt → teach#mission-interview-first
- `mission-shift-handling`: When the mission shifts or goes stale, confirm with the learner, revise the mission and add a learning record. — adopt → teach#mission-shift-handling
- `just-enough-knowledge`: Include only the knowledge a lesson's target skill needs, teaching it first and then practising. — defer
- `difficulty-by-kind`: Minimise difficulty when conveying knowledge but make retrieval effortful when building skills. — defer
- `skill-practice-forms`: Teach skills through quizzes, in-browser tasks or guided real-world step lists. — defer
- `community-opt-out`: Respect the learner's choice not to join communities and record it. — adopt → teach#community-opt-out
- `domain-vocabulary`: Use the project's established domain vocabulary throughout what you write. — adopt → teach#domain-vocabulary
- `learning-record-criteria`: Write a learning record only for demonstrated understanding, disclosed prior knowledge, a corrected misconception or a mission shift, never for coverage, glossary duplicates or activity logs. — adopt → teach#learning-record-criteria
- `field-term-resolution`: Record in the glossary how loosely used field terms are resolved in this workspace. — adopt → teach#field-term-resolution
- `in-place-definition-revision`: Revise glossary definitions in place as understanding deepens. — adopt → teach#in-place-definition-revision

- `glossary-entry-template`: Write glossary entries of a term and its definition, grouped under subheadings when clusters emerge. — adopt → teach#glossary-entry-template
- `canonical-term-and-aliases`: Pick one preferred term per concept and list its other words as aliases to avoid. — adopt → teach#canonical-term-and-aliases

- `glossary-self-vocabulary`: Use the glossary's own terms inside its other definitions. — adopt → teach#glossary-self-vocabulary

#### engineering · Intake · Triage — skill:skills/engineering/triage

- `no-stale-file-paths`: Keep concrete file paths out of a durable spec, ticket or brief, describing interfaces and behaviour that survive code drift. — defer
- `brief-behavioural`: Describe what the system should do, not how to implement it, leaving implementation choices to the executing agent. — adopt → triage#agent-ready-gate
- `brief-acceptance-criteria`: Give every brief concrete, independently testable acceptance criteria. — adopt → triage#brief-acceptance-criteria
- `brief-scope-boundaries`: State explicitly what is out of scope so the agent does not gold-plate. — adopt → triage#agent-ready-gate

- `pr-as-issue`: Treat an external pull request as an issue with attached code, running it through the same roles and state machine. — out-of-scope

- `natural-language-commands`: Interpret the maintainer's natural-language triage requests into the matching triage actions. — defer
- `pick-from-summary`: Show the count and a one-line summary of each waiting item and let the maintainer pick which to triage. — adopt → triage#pick-from-summary
- `read-full-source-issue`: Read the full body, comments and, for a pull request, the diff of any referenced spec, issue or pull request before working from it. — adopt → triage#read-full-source-issue
- `agent-brief-comment`: Post an agent brief as a comment on an item when it becomes ready for an agent. — defer
- `already-built-close`: Close a request that is already implemented by pointing to where it lives, recording no rejection. — adopt → triage#already-built-close
- `polite-bug-rejection`: Close a rejected bug report with a polite explanation of why. — out-of-scope
- `direct-move-shortcut`: On a direct instruction to move an item's state, confirm the actions and apply them without an interview. — defer
- `brief-offer-on-shortcut`: When moving an item to agent-ready without an interview, ask whether to write its agent brief. — defer
